agentic-coding/05-internet-web/access-co.title: access-control
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/access-co.content:
Access Control

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Rules defining who can access what. Read, write, execute permissions for each resource.
📋 Concrete Example
Access control: document grades.pdf: Alice (read, write), Bob (read), Carol (none). Each user has specific permissions for each resource. Enforced by the system.
🔗 Analogy
Access control is like room keycards in a school - students can enter classrooms, teachers can enter the staff room, the principal can enter anywhere. Each person has different access to different rooms.
Related Concepts

Authorization
Permission
Security

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/api-endpo.title: api-endpoint
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/api-endpo.content:
API Endpoint

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A specific URL where an API can be accessed. Each endpoint does one thing.
📋 Concrete Example
Endpoints: GET /api/users (list users), POST /api/users (create user), PUT /api/users/123 (update user 123), DELETE /api/users/123 (delete user 123). Each URL + method combination is an endpoint.
🔗 Analogy
An API endpoint is like a department in a store - ‘Customer Service’ handles returns, Cashier handles payments, Information handles questions. Each endpoint handles one type of request.
Related Concepts

API
REST API
HTTP Method

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/authentic.title: authentication
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/authentic.content:
Authentication

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Verifying who a user is. Usually with username + password, or tokens.
📋 Concrete Example
Authentication: user enters username alice and password secret123. Server checks: does this match the database? Yes. Authentication successful. User is Alice.
🔗 Analogy
Authentication is like showing your ID at a club - the bouncer checks your ID (password) against their records. If it matches, you are authenticated and can enter. The server authenticates users similarly.
Related Concepts

Session
Authorization
Token

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/authoriza.title: authorization
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/authoriza.content:
Authorization

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Checking what an authenticated user is allowed to do. Permissions and access control.
📋 Concrete Example
Authorization: Alice is authenticated. Can she delete users? Check permissions: Alice is admin -> yes. Bob is student -> no. Authorization determines what each user can do.
🔗 Analogy
Authorization is like keycard access in a hotel - your card (authentication) gets you into the building. But does it open the gym? The VIP lounge? The staff room? Authorization checks what your card allows.
Related Concepts

Authentication
Permission
Access Control

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/backend.title: backend
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/backend.content:
Backend

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The part of a web application that runs on the server: databases, business logic, APIs. The server side.
📋 Concrete Example
Backend: when user logs in, the backend: receives credentials, checks database, generates token, returns response. The user never sees this code. It runs on the server.
🔗 Analogy
The backend is like a restaurant’s kitchen - the customer (user) sees the dining area (frontend) but the cooking (business logic) happens in the kitchen (backend). The chef (server) prepares the food (data) and sends it out.
Related Concepts

Frontend
Full-Stack
API

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cdn.title: cdn
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cdn.content:
CDN

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Content Delivery Network - servers around the world that cache content close to users. Faster delivery.
📋 Concrete Example
CDN: your server is in Hong Kong. User in New York: 200ms latency. CDN has a copy in New York: 20ms latency. 10x faster. CDN caches content globally.
🔗 Analogy
A CDN is like franchise stores around the world - instead of buying from the one factory in Hong Kong (slow delivery), you buy from the local franchise (fast delivery). Same product, closer source.
Related Concepts

Web Server
Caching
Latency in Networks

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/component.title: component
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/component.content:
Component

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A reusable UI piece in frontend frameworks. Encapsulates HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
📋 Concrete Example
Component: <UserCard name=Alice avatar=pic.jpg />. Renders a card with Alice’s name and photo. Reuse: <UserCard name=Bob avatar=bob.jpg />. Same component, different data.
🔗 Analogy
A component is like a stamp - you design it once, then stamp it with different ink (data) on different papers (pages). Same design, different results. Components are reusable UI stamps.
Related Concepts

React
Frontend
Reusability

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/content-t.title: content-type
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/content-t.content:
Content-Type

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
An HTTP header that tells the receiver what format the data is in: JSON, HTML, image, etc.
📋 Concrete Example
Content-Type: application/json (data is JSON). text/html (data is HTML). image/png (data is a PNG image). The receiver knows how to parse the data based on this header.
🔗 Analogy
Content-Type is like a label on a package - Books (handle as books), ‘Perishable Food’ (handle as food), Electronics (handle as electronics). The label tells the receiver how to handle the contents.
Related Concepts

HTTP Header
JSON
HTML

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cookie.title: cookie
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cookie.content:
Cookie

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Small pieces of data stored in the browser. Used for sessions, preferences, and tracking.
📋 Concrete Example
Cookie: user logs in. Server sets cookie: session_id=abc123. Browser stores it. Next request: browser sends the cookie. Server knows who the user is. No need to log in again.
🔗 Analogy
A cookie is like a name tag - the server gives you a name tag (cookie) on your first visit. Every time you return, you wear the name tag. The server recognizes you immediately.
Related Concepts

Session
HTTP
Authentication

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cors.title: cors
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/cors.content:
CORS

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing - controls which websites can access your API. Security feature.
📋 Concrete Example
CORS: your API at api.example.com. Website at example.com can access it. Website at evil.com cannot. CORS prevents other websites from misusing your API.
🔗 Analogy
CORS is like a guest list at a party - only people on the list (allowed origins) can enter. Others are turned away. CORS ensures only authorized websites can access your API.
Related Concepts

Web API
Security
HTTP Header

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/css.title: css
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/css.content:
CSS

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Cascading Style Sheets - controls how web pages look: colors, fonts, layout, animation.
📋 Concrete Example
CSS: ‘h1 { color: blue; font-size: 24px; } .button { background: green; border-radius: 5px; }’. The browser applies these styles. Headings are blue, buttons are green with rounded corners.
🔗 Analogy
CSS is like interior design - the frame (HTML) is there, but CSS chooses the paint colors, furniture style, and lighting. Same frame, completely different look with different CSS.
Related Concepts

HTML
Web Browser
Responsive Design

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/csv.title: csv
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/csv.content:
CSV

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Comma-Separated Values - a simple data format. Each line is a row, columns separated by commas.
📋 Concrete Example
CSV: name,age,city\nAlice,14,Hong Kong\nBob,15,Tokyo\nCarol,16,Seoul. Simple, compact, opens in Excel. Good for tabular data.
🔗 Analogy
CSV is like a simple list on lined paper - each line is a row, columns separated by commas. No formatting, no complexity. Just data in rows and columns. Perfect for spreadsheets.
Related Concepts

Data Format
JSON
Spreadsheet

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/data-form.title: data-format
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/data-form.content:
Data Format

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
How data is structured for storage or transmission: JSON, XML, CSV, YAML. Each has different use cases.
📋 Concrete Example
JSON: web APIs. CSV: spreadsheets. XML: enterprise systems. YAML: configuration files. Each format structures data differently, optimized for different needs.
🔗 Analogy
Data formats are like different envelope types - business envelope (JSON) for letters, padded envelope (XML) for fragile items, large envelope (CSV) for bulk documents. Each format suits different data types.
Related Concepts

JSON
CSV
YAML

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dns-resol.title: dns-resolution
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dns-resol.content:
DNS Resolution

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The process of looking up a domain name’s IP address via DNS. Happens every time you visit a website.
📋 Concrete Example
DNS resolution: type google.com -> DNS server: ‘google.com is 142.250.80.46’ -> browser connects to that IP. Takes 1-10ms. Cached for future visits. Happens behind the scenes.
🔗 Analogy
DNS resolution is like looking up a phone number in your contacts - you type Mom -> contacts app shows her number -> you call. DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses the same way.
Related Concepts

DNS
Domain Name
Internet

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dom.title: dom
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dom.content:
DOM

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Document Object Model - the browser’s internal representation of a web page. JavaScript manipulates the DOM to change the page.
📋 Concrete Example
DOM: the browser parses HTML into a tree.  ->  -> , , . JavaScript: document.getElementById(myButton).innerHTML = ‘Clicked!’. The DOM tree is updated, and the page changes instantly.
🔗 Analogy
The DOM is like a blueprint of a house that the builder (browser) holds. JavaScript can modify the blueprint: ‘change this room’s color, add a door here.’ The builder immediately reflects the changes.
Related Concepts

HTML
JavaScript
Web Browser

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dynamic-s.title: dynamic-site
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/dynamic-s.content:
Dynamic Site

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A website with content generated on the server. Personalized, interactive, database-driven.
📋 Concrete Example
Dynamic site: you log in. Server: queries database, builds a personalized page with your name, recommendations, and history. Each user sees different content. Powered by a backend.
🔗 Analogy
A dynamic site is like a personal tutor - it adapts to each student. Different content for different people. Requires more processing (server) but provides personalized experiences.
Related Concepts

Web Development
Backend
Static Site

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/frontend.title: frontend
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/frontend.content:
Frontend

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The part of a web application users see and interact with: HTML, CSS, JavaScript. The client side.
📋 Concrete Example
Frontend: the login page - input fields, buttons, animations, error messages. Everything the user sees and clicks. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript (or frameworks like React).
🔗 Analogy
The frontend is like a restaurant’s dining area - the decor, menu, tables, and waiters. Everything the customer sees and interacts with. The kitchen (backend) is behind the scenes.
Related Concepts

Backend
Full-Stack
React

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/full-stac.title: full-stack
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/full-stac.content:
Full-Stack

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A developer who works on both frontend and backend. Full-stack agents can build entire web applications.
📋 Concrete Example
Full-stack agent: builds the frontend (React UI), backend (Flask API), and database (PostgreSQL). It handles everything from button clicks to data storage.
🔗 Analogy
A full-stack developer is like a solo restaurant owner - they cook (backend), serve (frontend), manage inventory (database), and clean up (DevOps). They do everything, end to end.
Related Concepts

Frontend
Backend
Web Development

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/html-pars.title: html-parsing
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/html-pars.content:
HTML Parsing

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Reading HTML and extracting specific elements: text, links, images. Done with tools like BeautifulSoup.
📋 Concrete Example
Parsing: BeautifulSoup(html, html.parser).find_all(a) -> extract all links. Or find_all(p, class_=article) -> extract article paragraphs. Convert raw HTML into structured data.
🔗 Analogy
HTML parsing is like reading a textbook with a highlighter - you scan the pages (HTML) and highlight specific parts (elements). You convert a wall of text into organized, useful information.
Related Concepts

Web Scraping
HTML
DOM

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/html.title: html
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/html.content:
HTML

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
HyperText Markup Language - the structure of web pages. Tags define headings, paragraphs, links, images.
📋 Concrete Example
HTML: ‘WelcomeThis is a paragraph.Link’. The browser reads these tags and displays: a heading, a paragraph, and a clickable link.
🔗 Analogy
HTML is like the frame of a house - it defines rooms (sections), doors (links), and windows (images). The frame gives structure. CSS paints the walls; JavaScript adds electricity.
Related Concepts

Web Browser
CSS
DOM

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/http-head.title: http-header
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/http-head.content:
HTTP Header

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Metadata sent with HTTP requests and responses: content type, authentication, caching, CORS.
📋 Concrete Example
Headers: ‘Content-Type: application/json’ (data is JSON). ‘Authorization: Bearer token123’ (authenticated). ‘Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *’ (CORS: any website can access). Metadata about the request.
🔗 Analogy
HTTP headers are like labels on a package - Fragile (handle carefully), Refrigerate (storage instruction), ‘Return Address’ (sender). Headers give the server instructions about how to handle the request.
Related Concepts

HTTP
CORS
Content-Type

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/http-meth.title: http-method
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/http-meth.content:
HTTP Method

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Verbs that define what to do with a resource: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE (remove).
📋 Concrete Example
GET /users: list all users. POST /users: create a new user. PUT /users/123: update user 123. DELETE /users/123: delete user 123. The method tells the server what action to perform.
🔗 Analogy
HTTP methods are like verbs in a sentence - GET (read), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE (destroy). The resource (users) is the noun. Together, they form a complete instruction.
Related Concepts

REST API
HTTP
API Endpoint

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/internet.title: internet
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/internet.content:
Internet

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The internet connects billions of devices worldwide. Understanding it is essential because AI agents live on the internet - they fetch data, call APIs, and serve users globally.
📋 Concrete Example
You type google.com. Your request travels through undersea cables, reaches Google’s server, and returns results in 50ms. The internet makes this possible for billions of people simultaneously.
🔗 Analogy
The internet is like a global postal system - your letter (data) goes from your house to a post office (router) to another post office to the destination. Billions of letters travel simultaneously, each reaching the right address.
Related Concepts

Network
TCP-IP
World Wide Web

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/javascrip.title: javascript
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/javascrip.content:
JavaScript

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The programming language of the web. Runs in the browser. Adds interactivity: clicks, animations, dynamic content.
📋 Concrete Example
JavaScript: button.addEventListener(click, () => { alert(‘Hello!’); }). When the user clicks the button, a popup appears. JavaScript makes web pages interactive, not just static.
🔗 Analogy
JavaScript is like electricity in a house - the frame (HTML) and decoration (CSS) are static. Electricity (JS) makes things move: lights turn on, the doorbell rings, the TV works. JavaScript brings web pages to life.
Related Concepts

HTML
Web Browser
DOM

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/json.title: json
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/json.content:
JSON

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
JavaScript Object Notation - a lightweight data format. The standard for API data exchange.
📋 Concrete Example
JSON: {“name”: “Alice”, “age”: 14, “hobbies”: [“coding”, “gaming”]}. Easy for humans to read, easy for machines to parse. The lingua franca of web APIs.
🔗 Analogy
JSON is like a standardized form - everyone fills it out the same way: name, age, hobbies. Any system can read it. JSON is the standard form for data exchange on the web.
Related Concepts

REST API
API
Data Format

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/jwt.title: jwt
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/jwt.content:
JWT

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
JSON Web Token - a standard for tokens. Contains user info, signed for security.
📋 Concrete Example
JWT: three parts - header, payload, signature. Payload: {user_id: 123, role: admin, exp: 1690000000}. Signature: verifies it has not been tampered with. Compact, self-contained, widely used.
🔗 Analogy
JWT is like a sealed letter of recommendation - it contains information about you (payload), is sealed by the sender (signature), and anyone can verify the seal. No one can tamper with it without breaking the seal.
Related Concepts

Token
Authentication
JSON

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/nginx.title: nginx
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/nginx.content:
Nginx

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A popular web server and reverse proxy. Handles high traffic efficiently. Used for load balancing and serving static files.
📋 Concrete Example
Nginx: receives 10,000 requests/second. Serves static files (images, CSS) directly - fast. For dynamic content, forwards to the backend application. Also load balances across multiple backend instances.
🔗 Analogy
Nginx is like an efficient traffic cop - they handle simple requests (static files) themselves instantly. Complex requests (dynamic content) are forwarded to specialists (backend). They also direct traffic to less busy lanes (load balancing).
Related Concepts

Web Server
Load Balancer
Reverse Proxy

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/offline-m.title: offline-mode
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/offline-m.content:
Offline Mode

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
When a web app works without internet. Achieved through caching and service workers.
📋 Concrete Example
Offline mode: you open the app. No internet. The service worker serves cached files. You can read saved articles, see cached data. When internet returns, the app syncs.
🔗 Analogy
Offline mode is like a downloaded movie - you download it once (online), then watch it anytime (offline). No internet needed. Offline mode lets web apps work like downloaded content.
Related Concepts

Service Worker
Progressive Web App
Caching

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/paginatio.title: pagination
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/paginatio.content:
Pagination

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Splitting large lists into pages. API returns 20 items per page instead of 10,000 at once.
📋 Concrete Example
Pagination: GET /api/users?page=2&per_page=20. Returns users 21-40. Not all 10,000 at once. Faster, less memory, better UX. User clicks Next for page 3.
🔗 Analogy
Pagination is like pages in a book - instead of one long scroll (10,000 items), you have pages (20 items each). Easier to read, faster to load. You turn pages instead of scrolling endlessly.
Related Concepts

REST API
JSON
User Experience

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/progressi.title: progressive-web-app
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/progressi.content:
Progressive Web App

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A web app that works like a native app: offline, push notifications, home screen icon.
📋 Concrete Example
PWA: you visit a website. Browser asks: ‘Add to home screen?’ You accept. Now it has an icon, works offline, and sends push notifications - like a real app. But it is still a website.
🔗 Analogy
A PWA is like a food truck that becomes a restaurant - it starts mobile (website) but can set up a permanent location (home screen), serve customers even when the road is closed (offline), and send promotions (push notifications).
Related Concepts

Responsive Design
Web Development
Service Worker

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rate-limi.title: rate-limiting
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rate-limi.content:
Rate Limiting

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Restricting how many API requests a user can make per time period. Prevents abuse.
📋 Concrete Example
Rate limit: 100 requests per minute per user. User A: 50 requests -> OK. User A: 101st request -> ‘429 Too Many Requests.’ Prevents abuse and ensures fair usage.
🔗 Analogy
Rate limiting is like a speed limit on a highway - you can only go 80 km/h, not 200. It prevents dangerous behavior and ensures everyone gets fair use of the road. Rate limiting ensures fair API access.
Related Concepts

API
Security
Throttling

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/react.title: react
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/react.content:
React

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A JavaScript library for building user interfaces. Component-based, declarative. Very popular.
📋 Concrete Example
React: build a Button component. Reuse it everywhere: <Button color=red onClick={handleClick}>. Components are like Lego bricks - build once, reuse everywhere. React manages the UI efficiently.
🔗 Analogy
React is like Lego - you build small pieces (components) and combine them into complex structures (UIs). Each piece is reusable. Change one piece, and React efficiently updates only what changed.
Related Concepts

Frontend
Component
Virtual DOM

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/real-time.title: real-time-communication
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/real-time.content:
Real-Time Communication

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Exchanging data instantly, with minimal delay. Chat, gaming, live streaming, collaborative editing.
📋 Concrete Example
Real-time: you type a message. Your friend sees it in 50ms. You move a game character. Other players see it instantly. No page refresh, no delay. WebSocket enables this.
🔗 Analogy
Real-time communication is like a walkie-talkie - you speak and the other person hears instantly. No waiting, no delays. Essential for chat, gaming, and live collaboration.
Related Concepts

WebSocket
Latency in Networks
Streaming

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rendering.title: rendering
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rendering.content:
Rendering

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The process of generating the visual output from code. Browser rendering: HTML + CSS -> pixels on screen.
📋 Concrete Example
Rendering: browser receives HTML, builds DOM tree. Applies CSS styles. Lays out elements. Paints pixels on screen. 60 times per second for smooth animation. The browser’s core job.
🔗 Analogy
Rendering is like a painter translating a sketch into a finished painting - they take the outline (HTML), apply colors (CSS), and produce the final artwork (pixels on screen). The browser renders web pages.
Related Concepts

Web Browser
Virtual DOM
CSS

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/responsiv.title: responsive-design
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/responsiv.content:
Responsive Design

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Designing websites that work on all screen sizes: phone, tablet, desktop.
📋 Concrete Example
Responsive: CSS media queries: ‘@media (max-width: 768px) { .menu { display: none; } }’. On mobile, the menu is hidden; a hamburger icon appears. On desktop, the full menu shows. One website, all devices.
🔗 Analogy
Responsive design is like a transformer toy - it changes shape depending on the situation. On a small screen (phone), it is compact. On a large screen (desktop), it expands. Same toy, different forms.
Related Concepts

CSS
Frontend
Mobile Design

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rest-api.title: rest-api
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/rest-api.content:
REST API

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Representational State Transfer - a style of API design using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) on resources.
📋 Concrete Example
REST API: GET /books (list), POST /books (create), GET /books/123 (detail), PUT /books/123 (update), DELETE /books/123 (delete). Standard, predictable, widely used.
🔗 Analogy
REST is like a library system - GET (read a book), POST (add a new book), PUT (update a book), DELETE (remove a book). Standard operations on resources (books). Clear and predictable.
Related Concepts

API Endpoint
HTTP Method
JSON

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/reverse-p.title: reverse-proxy
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/reverse-p.content:
Reverse Proxy

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A server that sits in front of other servers, forwarding requests. Provides security, load balancing, and caching.
📋 Concrete Example
Reverse proxy: all requests go to proxy.example.com. Proxy forwards to backend1, backend2, or backend3. Users never see the backend servers directly. Security + load balancing + caching.
🔗 Analogy
A reverse proxy is like a building receptionist - all visitors go to reception first. Reception directs them to the right office (backend server). Visitors never know the actual office number. Security and organization.
Related Concepts

Nginx
Load Balancer
Web Server

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/service-w.title: service-worker
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/service-w.content:
Service Worker

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A script that runs in the background, enabling offline functionality, push notifications, and caching for PWAs.
📋 Concrete Example
Service worker: intercepts network requests. If offline: serves cached files. If online: fetches fresh data. Runs even when the page is closed. Enables push notifications.
🔗 Analogy
A service worker is like a night security guard - they work even when the store (page) is closed. They handle incoming requests (visitors), check inventory (cache), and call for backup (fetch from network) when needed.
Related Concepts

Progressive Web App
Caching
Offline Mode

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/session.title: session
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/session.content:
Session

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A period of interaction between user and server. The server remembers the user across multiple requests.
📋 Concrete Example
Session: user logs in at 2pm. Session starts. User browses for 30 minutes. Server remembers: this is Alice, she is logged in, she has items in her cart. Session ends at 2:30pm (timeout or logout).
🔗 Analogy
A session is like a gym membership - you check in (login), use the gym (browse), and the staff knows who you are the whole time. When you leave (logout), the session ends. Next visit, you check in again.
Related Concepts

Cookie
Authentication
State Management

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/single-pa.title: single-page-application
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/single-pa.content:
Single Page Application

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A web app that loads once and updates dynamically without page reloads. Smooth, app-like experience.
📋 Concrete Example
SPA: you click Profile. Instead of loading a new page, JavaScript: 1) fetches profile data (API). 2) Updates the DOM. 3) URL changes to /profile. No page reload. Smooth, instant.
🔗 Analogy
SPA is like a magic book - you turn to a new chapter, but the book does not close and reopen. The content changes instantly. No loading screen. Smooth transitions between pages.
Related Concepts

React
Frontend
Virtual DOM

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/ssl-certi.title: ssl-certificate
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/ssl-certi.content:
SSL Certificate

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A digital certificate that proves a website’s identity and enables HTTPS encryption.
📋 Concrete Example
SSL certificate: issued by a Certificate Authority. Contains: domain name, owner, expiration. Browser checks: is this certificate valid? Yes -> shows the lock icon. No -> warns the user.
🔗 Analogy
An SSL certificate is like a passport - it proves identity (this is really google.com) and is issued by a trusted authority (Certificate Authority). The browser checks it, just like immigration checks your passport.
Related Concepts

TLS
HTTPS
Security

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/static-si.title: static-site
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/static-si.content:
Static Site

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A website with fixed content. No server-side processing. Fast, cheap, secure.
📋 Concrete Example
Static site: HTML, CSS, JS files on a server. No database, no server code. Just files. Extremely fast (no processing), cheap (no server needed), secure (no server to hack). Good for blogs and portfolios.
🔗 Analogy
A static site is like a printed brochure - the content is fixed. Everyone sees the same thing. No interactivity, but fast, cheap, and reliable. Contrast with a dynamic site, which is like a live conversation.
Related Concepts

Web Development
Frontend
Dynamic Site

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/streaming.title: streaming
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/streaming.content:
Streaming

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Sending data continuously rather than all at once. Used for video, audio, and AI token streaming.
📋 Concrete Example
Streaming: instead of waiting for the full AI response (10 seconds), stream tokens as they are generated. User sees words appearing one by one. Feels instant, even though total time is the same.
🔗 Analogy
Streaming is like a water tap - instead of delivering a bucket of water all at once, water flows continuously. You start drinking immediately. Streaming delivers data continuously for a better experience.
Related Concepts

Real-Time Communication
Token Stream
Latency in Networks

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/token-str.title: token-stream
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/token-str.content:
Token Stream

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
When an LLM generates tokens one at a time and sends each immediately. The user sees text appearing progressively.
📋 Concrete Example
Token stream: model generates The -> send. ’ capital’ -> send. ’ of’ -> send. ’ France’ -> send. ’ is’ -> send. ’ Paris.’ -> send. User sees the sentence building up, word by word. Feels faster.
🔗 Analogy
Token streaming is like a typist typing a letter while you watch - each letter appears as they type. You start reading immediately, before the letter is finished. Token streaming shows AI output as it is generated.
Related Concepts

Streaming
Next-Token Prediction
User Experience

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/token.title: token
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/token.content:
Token

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A piece of data that proves authentication. Sent with each request instead of re-entering passwords.
📋 Concrete Example
Token: after login, server gives a JWT token: eyJhbG.... Client stores it. Each API request includes the token. Server verifies: is this token valid? Yes -> authenticated. No -> rejected.
🔗 Analogy
A token is like a festival wristband - you show your ticket once (login), get a wristband (token). For the rest of the festival, you just show the wristband. No need to show your ticket again. Tokens work the same way.
Related Concepts

Authentication
JWT
Session

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/virtual-d.title: virtual-dom
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/virtual-d.content:
Virtual DOM

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
React’s internal representation of the DOM. Enables efficient UI updates by comparing changes.
📋 Concrete Example
Virtual DOM: React keeps a copy of the DOM in memory. When data changes, React: 1) updates the virtual DOM. 2) Compares with the real DOM. 3) Updates only the changed parts. Efficient.
🔗 Analogy
The virtual DOM is like a draft blueprint - the architect (React) sketches changes on a draft first, compares with the current blueprint, and only sends the differences to the builder (browser). Efficient, no wasted work.
Related Concepts

React
DOM
Rendering

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-api.title: web-api
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-api.content:
Web API

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
An API accessed over HTTP. The most common way for applications to communicate on the internet.
📋 Concrete Example
Web API: your app calls ‘GET api.weather.com/today’. Returns JSON: {temp: 28, condition: sunny}. Your app uses this data to show weather. APIs connect applications.
🔗 Analogy
A web API is like a restaurant’s takeout window - you (application) ask for food (data) through the window (API). The kitchen (server) prepares it and hands it out. You do not need to go inside.
Related Concepts

REST API
API Endpoint
JSON

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-brows.title: web-browser
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-brows.content:
Web Browser

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A program that fetches and displays web pages. Chrome, Safari, Firefox are browsers.
📋 Concrete Example
Browser: you type google.com. Browser sends HTTP request, receives HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and renders the page. It interprets the code and displays the visual result.
🔗 Analogy
A web browser is like a translator and decorator - it fetches raw materials (HTML, CSS, JS) from a server, translates them, and presents a beautifully decorated page. Without the browser, web code is just text.
Related Concepts

World Wide Web
HTML
Rendering

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-devel.title: web-development
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-devel.content:
Web Development

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Building websites and web applications. Involves frontend, backend, databases, and deployment.
📋 Concrete Example
Web development: 1) Design UI (frontend). 2) Build API (backend). 3) Set up database. 4) Deploy to server. 5) Maintain and update. The full process of creating a web application.
🔗 Analogy
Web development is like building a house - design the layout (frontend), install plumbing and electricity (backend), set up storage (database), get permits (deployment), and maintain it. A complete construction project.
Related Concepts

Full-Stack
Frontend
Backend

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-scrap.title: web-scraping
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-scrap.content:
Web Scraping

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Extracting data from web pages by parsing HTML. Useful when no API is available.
📋 Concrete Example
Scraping: fetch ‘news.com’, parse HTML, extract all  tags (headlines). Return: [‘AI Breakthrough’, ‘New Phone Released’, …]. Get data from any website, even without an API.
🔗 Analogy
Web scraping is like clipping newspaper articles - you go to the newsstand (website), find the articles you want (headlines), and clip them (extract). No subscription (API) needed, but you must do the work yourself.
Related Concepts

HTML Parsing
Web API
Data Collection

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-serve.title: web-server
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/web-serve.content:
Web Server

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
Software that receives HTTP requests and sends HTTP responses. Apache, Nginx are web servers.
📋 Concrete Example
Web server: receives ‘GET /index.html’. Finds the file. Sends ‘200 OK’ + HTML. Receives ‘GET /api/data’. Calls the application. Sends JSON. The middleman between client and application.
🔗 Analogy
A web server is like a restaurant host - they greet customers (requests), find them a table (route to the right resource), and bring the menu (response). They handle the flow of customers.
Related Concepts

HTTP
Backend
Nginx

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/webhook.title: webhook
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/webhook.content:
Webhook

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A URL that receives HTTP POST requests when an event occurs. Like a callback for web services.
📋 Concrete Example
Webhook: when a GitHub push happens, GitHub sends a POST to your webhook URL: yourapp.com/webhook. Your app receives it and triggers a build. Automated, event-driven.
🔗 Analogy
A webhook is like an automatic phone call from a store - ‘Your order is ready.’ You do not need to call and ask; they call you when it is ready. Webhooks call your app when events happen.
Related Concepts

HTTP
Event-Driven Architecture
API

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/websocket.title: websocket
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/websocket.content:
WebSocket

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
A protocol for real-time, two-way communication between client and server. Unlike HTTP, the connection stays open.
📋 Concrete Example
WebSocket: chat app. Client connects to server. Connection stays open. Client sends message -> server receives instantly. Server sends new message -> client receives instantly. Real-time, bidirectional.
🔗 Analogy
WebSocket is like a phone call - once connected, both sides can talk anytime. No need to dial again. HTTP is like a text message - each message is separate. WebSocket keeps the line open for real-time chat.
Related Concepts

HTTP
Real-Time Communication
Socket

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/world-wid.title: world-wide-web
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/world-wid.content:
World Wide Web

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
The Web is the part of the internet accessed through browsers. Websites, web apps, and web APIs. Not the same as the internet (which also includes email, gaming, etc.).
📋 Concrete Example
The internet: roads, bridges, tunnels. The Web: shops and buildings on those roads. Email, online games, and file transfers use the internet but are not the Web.
🔗 Analogy
The internet is the road network; the Web is the buildings along the roads. You use roads (internet) to reach buildings (websites). But roads also reach places that are not buildings (email servers, game servers).
Related Concepts

Internet
HTTP
Web Browser

agentic-coding/05-internet-web/yaml.title: yaml
agentic-coding/05-internet-web/yaml.content:
YAML

Domain: Internet & Web

🎯 Motivation
YAML Ain’t Markup Language - a human-friendly data format used for configuration files.
📋 Concrete Example
YAML: name: Alice\nage: 14\nhobbies:\n  - coding\n  - gaming. Clean, readable, uses indentation for structure. Common for config files and CI-CD pipelines.
🔗 Analogy
YAML is like a neatly organized outline - indentation shows hierarchy, no brackets or commas. Clean and readable. Perfect for configuration files that humans need to read and edit.
Related Concepts

Data Format
JSON
Configuration
