Vector
Tensor
Matrix Multiplication

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/maximum-lik.title: maximum-likelihood
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/maximum-lik.content:
Maximum Likelihood

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Choose parameters that make the observed data most probable. The principle behind many ML training procedures.
📋 Concrete Example
If data looks bell-shaped, pick the mean and variance that make that bell curve fit best.
🔗 Analogy
Like a detective picking the story that best explains all the evidence - the most likely scenario.
Related Concepts

Probability
Optimization
Loss Function

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mean-square.title: mean-squared-error
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mean-square.content:
Mean Squared Error

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The average of squared errors. Penalizes large errors more than small ones.
📋 Concrete Example
Errors of 2 and 4: squared to 4 and 16, averaged to 10. The 4-error dominates.
🔗 Analogy
Like a test that punishes big mistakes extra hard - a 10-point miss hurts more than five 2-point misses.
Related Concepts

Loss Function
Variance
Regression

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mean.title: mean
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mean.content:
Mean

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The average of a set of numbers. The simplest summary of the center of data.
📋 Concrete Example
Scores [70, 80, 90]. Mean = (70+80+90)/3 = 80.
🔗 Analogy
Like sharing all the class candy equally - everyone gets the average amount.
Related Concepts

Median
Mode
Statistics

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/median.title: median
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/median.content:
Median

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The middle value when data is sorted. Not affected by extreme outliers.
📋 Concrete Example
Salaries sorted: [10k, 20k, 25k, 30k, 1M]. Median = 25k. Mean would be dragged up by the 1M.
🔗 Analogy
Like the middle person in a line sorted by height - one giant at the end does not change them.
Related Concepts

Mean
Mode
Statistics

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mode.title: mode
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/mode.content:
Mode

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The most frequently occurring value in a dataset.
📋 Concrete Example
Shoe sizes sold: [36, 37, 38, 38, 38, 39]. Mode = 38 because it appears most.
🔗 Analogy
Like the most popular dish at a canteen - the one ordered most often.
Related Concepts

Mean
Median
Statistics

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/norm.title: norm
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/norm.content:
Norm

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The length or magnitude of a vector. L2 norm is the Euclidean length; L1 norm is the sum of absolute values.
📋 Concrete Example
L2 norm of [3, 4] = 5. L1 norm of [3, 4] = 7.
🔗 Analogy
Like measuring the total length of a route - L2 is the crow-flies distance, L1 is the city-block distance.
Related Concepts

Vector
Euclidean Distance
L1 L2 Regularization

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/normal-dist.title: normal-distribution
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/normal-dist.content:
Normal Distribution

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The bell curve. Most data clusters around the mean, with fewer values at the extremes.
📋 Concrete Example
Heights of students: most near the average, few very short or very tall. Classic bell shape.
🔗 Analogy
Like a sand pile - most sand heaps in the middle, with thinner slopes on the sides.
Related Concepts

Uniform Distribution
Mean
Standard Deviation

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/one-hot-enc.title: one-hot-encoding
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/one-hot-enc.content:
One-Hot Encoding

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Represents a category as a vector with a single 1 and the rest 0s. Lets models handle categorical data.
📋 Concrete Example
Three colors red, green, blue become [1,0,0], [0,1,0], [0,0,1]. No implied ordering.
🔗 Analogy
Like a multiple choice answer sheet - you fill exactly one bubble, leaving the rest blank.
Related Concepts

Softmax
Classification
Cross-Entropy

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/optimizatio.title: optimization
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/optimizatio.content:
Optimization

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Finding the best solution from many options. Training a model is an optimization problem.
📋 Concrete Example
Gradient descent optimizes weights to minimize the loss function.
🔗 Analogy
Like tuning a radio dial to find the clearest signal among many positions.
Related Concepts

Gradient Descent
Loss Function
Convex Function

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/partial-der.title: partial-derivative
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/partial-der.content:
Partial Derivative

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The derivative with respect to one variable while keeping others fixed. Used when functions have many inputs.
📋 Concrete Example
For f(x, y) = x*y, partial derivative with respect to x is y (treat y as constant).

Like adjusting only the volume on a mixing desk while leaving all other sliders alone, to see the effect.
Related Concepts

Gradient
Derivative
Gradient Descent

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/probability.title: probability
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/probability.content:
Probability

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Measures how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). The language of uncertainty in AI.
📋 Concrete Example
The probability of rolling a 6 on a fair die is 1/6, about 0.167.
🔗 Analogy
Like a weather forecast saying 70% chance of rain - a number between 0 and 1 for how likely.
Related Concepts

Conditional Probability
Bayes Theorem
Distribution

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/relu.title: relu
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/relu.content:
ReLU

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Max(0, x). Simple, fast, and avoids the vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs.
📋 Concrete Example
ReLU(5)=5, ReLU(-3)=0. Gradient is 1 for positive, 0 for negative.

Like a one-way valve - positive flow passes through unchanged, negative flow is blocked.
Related Concepts

Activation Function
Vanishing Gradient
Neural Network

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sampling.title: sampling
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sampling.content:
Sampling

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Picking items from a distribution. Used to generate text, augment data, and estimate statistics.
📋 Concrete Example
A language model samples the next word from its probability distribution, adding variety to outputs.
🔗 Analogy
Like drawing names from a hat - you pick one based on the probabilities, not always the most likely.
Related Concepts

Probability
Distribution
Language Model

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/set-theory.title: set-theory
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/set-theory.content:
Set Theory

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The study of collections of objects. Foundation for logic, probability, and data operations.
📋 Concrete Example
The set of students who like math intersected with the set who like music gives students who like both.
🔗 Analogy
Like sorting toys into labeled boxes and then finding what is in common or different between boxes.
Related Concepts

Logic
Probability

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sigmoid-der.title: sigmoid-derivative
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sigmoid-der.content:
Sigmoid Derivative

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The slope of sigmoid, used in backpropagation. Maxes at 0.25, which causes vanishing gradients in deep networks.
📋 Concrete Example
Sigmoid derivative at x=0 is 0.25 (steepest). At extremes it approaches 0, meaning gradients vanish.
🔗 Analogy
Like a hill that is flattest at the top and bottom - hard to slide down when there is no slope.

Sigmoid
Derivative
Vanishing Gradient

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sigmoid.title: sigmoid
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/sigmoid.content:
Sigmoid

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Squashes any real number into (0, 1). Historically popular, now mostly replaced by ReLU in hidden layers.
📋 Concrete Example
Sigmoid(0) = 0.5. Very positive input goes to ~1, very negative goes to ~0.
🔗 Analogy
Like a dimmer switch smoothly going from off (0) to fully on (1).
Related Concepts

Activation Function
Softmax
Logistic Regression

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/softmax.title: softmax
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/softmax.content:
Softmax

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Converts a vector of scores into probabilities that sum to 1. The standard output for multi-class classification.
📋 Concrete Example
Scores [1, 2, 3] become probabilities [0.09, 0.24, 0.67] after softmax. The biggest score gets the most probability.
🔗 Analogy
Like an election that converts vote counts into percentages - all percentages add up to 100%.
Related Concepts

Sigmoid
Cross-Entropy
Classification

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/standard-de.title: standard-deviation
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/standard-de.content:
Standard Deviation

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The square root of variance, in the same units as the data. Easier to interpret.
📋 Concrete Example
If variance is 25, standard deviation is 5. Most data falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean.
🔗 Analogy
Like a margin of error - plus or minus 5 marks tells you how spread out exam scores typically are.
Related Concepts

Variance
Mean
Normal Distribution

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/statistics.title: statistics
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/statistics.content:
Statistics

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
The science of collecting, summarizing, and interpreting data. Essential for understanding ML results.
📋 Concrete Example
Computing mean, median, and standard deviation of student test scores to understand class performance.
🔗 Analogy
Like a sports commentator summarizing a match with stats - possession, shots, passes - to tell the story.
Related Concepts

Mean
Variance
Probability
Distribution

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/tensor.title: tensor
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/tensor.content:
Tensor

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
A generalization of vectors and matrices to any number of dimensions. The data format deep learning uses.
📋 Concrete Example
A color image is a 3D tensor: height x width x 3 color channels (RGB). A batch of 32 images is a 4D tensor.
🔗 Analogy
Like a cube of data, or even a hypercube - you can keep adding dimensions as needed.
Related Concepts

Vector
Matrix
Neural Network

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/uniform-dis.title: uniform-distribution
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/uniform-dis.content:
Uniform Distribution

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Every outcome has equal probability. No value is more likely than another.
📋 Concrete Example
Rolling a fair 6-sided die: each face has exactly 1/6 chance. Flat, not bell-shaped.
🔗 Analogy
Like a lottery where every ticket has the same chance of winning - no favorites.
Related Concepts

Normal Distribution
Probability

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/vanishing-g.title: vanishing-gradient
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/vanishing-g.content:
Vanishing Gradient

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
When gradients shrink to near zero as they propagate back through layers, stopping deep networks from learning.
📋 Concrete Example
In a 20-layer network with sigmoid, gradients in early layers may be 0.25 to the power 20, essentially zero.
🔗 Analogy
Like a whisper passed through 20 people - by the end, the message has faded to nothing.
Related Concepts

Sigmoid Derivative
Backpropagation
Deep Learning
ReLU

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/variance.title: variance
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/variance.content:
Variance

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
Measures how spread out the data is from the mean. High variance means data is scattered widely.
📋 Concrete Example
Two classes both average 70. Class A scores range 65-75 (low variance). Class B ranges 40-100 (high variance).
🔗 Analogy
Like measuring how far arrows spread from the bullseye - tight cluster is low variance, scattered is high.
Related Concepts

Standard Deviation
Mean
Statistics

agentic-coding/08-math-logic/vector.title: vector
agentic-coding/08-math-logic/vector.content:
Vector

Domain: Math & Logic for AI

🎯 Motivation
A list of numbers that represents a point or direction in space. The basic building block of data in AI.
📋 Concrete Example
A student can be represented as a vector: [Math=85, English=72, Science=90]. Each number is a feature.
🔗 Analogy
Like a GPS coordinate with three numbers (lat, long, altitude) that pinpoints a spot.
Related Concepts

Matrix
Tensor
Dot Product
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/attention-mechanis.title: attention-mechanism
agentic-coding/09-nlp/attention-mechanis.content:
Attention Mechanism

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Lets the model focus on the most relevant input words when producing each output word.
📋 Concrete Example
Translating The bank of the river, attention links bank to river (not to money-bank) to translate correctly.
🔗 Analogy
Like a student highlighting key sentences in a textbook before answering a question.
Related Concepts

Self-Attention
Transformer Architecture
Machine Translation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/bag-of-words.title: bag-of-words
agentic-coding/09-nlp/bag-of-words.content:
Bag of Words

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Represents text as a count of each word, ignoring order. Simple but loses meaning and structure.
📋 Concrete Example
I love AI and AI loves me becomes {I:1, love:1, AI:2, and:1, loves:1, me:1}. Order is gone.
🔗 Analogy
Like tossing all words from a sentence into a bag - you know what words are there but not the order.
Related Concepts

N-Gram
TF-IDF
Vectorization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/beam-search.title: beam-search
agentic-coding/09-nlp/beam-search.content:
Beam Search

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
At each step, keeps the top K most promising partial outputs instead of just the best one. Improves generation.
📋 Concrete Example
With beam width 3, the decoder keeps 3 best partial translations at each step and expands all of them.
🔗 Analogy
Like a chess player thinking several moves ahead and keeping multiple promising lines of play.
Related Concepts

Greedy Decoding
Decoder
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/bert.title: bert
agentic-coding/09-nlp/bert.content:
BERT

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Reads text in both directions for deep understanding.
📋 Concrete Example
BERT is trained with masked language modeling. It is great for classification and question answering, not generation.
🔗 Analogy
Like a reader who can look at the whole page at once, both left and right, to understand each word.
Related Concepts

Masked Language Modeling
Encoder
Transformer Architecture

agentic-coding/09-nlp/bleu-score.title: bleu-score
agentic-coding/09-nlp/bleu-score.content:
BLEU Score

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Measures how close machine translation output is to human reference translations. Higher is better.
📋 Concrete Example
If the model output matches the reference exactly, BLEU = 1.0. Partial matches give partial scores.
🔗 Analogy
Like grading a translation essay by comparing it to the teacher reference answer.
Related Concepts

Evaluation
Machine Translation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/bpe.title: bpe
agentic-coding/09-nlp/bpe.content:
BPE

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Byte-Pair Encoding starts with characters and merges the most frequent pairs step by step. Used by GPT models.
📋 Concrete Example
Start with characters. low + est merge to lowest if seen often. Build a vocabulary of frequent subwords.
🔗 Analogy
Like a factory that starts with tiny parts and keeps gluing the most common pairs together until it has useful modules.
Related Concepts

Subword Tokenization
WordPiece
Vocabulary
Tokenization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/causal-language-mo.title: causal-language-modeling
agentic-coding/09-nlp/causal-language-mo.content:
Causal Language Modeling

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Predicts the next token given all previous tokens. How GPT models are trained.
📋 Concrete Example
Given The cat sat on the, predict mat. The model can only look left, never right.
🔗 Analogy
Like writing a story one word at a time - you can only use what you have already written.
Related Concepts

Language Model
GPT
Next Token Prediction
Decoder

agentic-coding/09-nlp/character-level-to.title: character-level-tokenization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/character-level-to.content:
Character-Level Tokenization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Splits text into individual characters. No out-of-vocabulary problem, but sequences get very long.
📋 Concrete Example
AI becomes [A, I]. Every character is a token.
🔗 Analogy
Like spelling out a word letter by letter - no word is unknown, but it takes a long time to say.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Word Tokenization
Subword Tokenization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/chunking.title: chunking
agentic-coding/09-nlp/chunking.content:
Chunking

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Grouping tokens into meaningful phrases (noun phrases, verb phrases). A step between tokens and full parsing.
📋 Concrete Example
The big red car becomes [The big red car] as one noun phrase chunk.
🔗 Analogy
Like grouping words into Lego blocks - each block is a phrase you can move around.
Related Concepts

Part of Speech Tagging
Syntax
Tokenization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/context-length.title: context-length
agentic-coding/09-nlp/context-length.content:
Context Length

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
How many tokens of conversation the model remembers at once. Beyond this, old messages are forgotten.
📋 Concrete Example
If context length is 4096 tokens and the chat exceeds that, the earliest messages drop out of memory.
🔗 Analogy
Like a goldfish bowl - there is only so much room. New water pushes old water out.
Related Concepts

Context Window
Tokenization
Transformer Architecture

agentic-coding/09-nlp/context-window.title: context-window
agentic-coding/09-nlp/context-window.content:
Context Window

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The maximum number of tokens a model can see at once. Larger windows mean longer memory but more cost.
📋 Concrete Example
GPT-4 has a 128K token context window. It can read a whole short book, but not a full library.
🔗 Analogy
Like the size of your desk - you can only work with the documents that fit on it at one time.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Transformer Architecture
Attention

agentic-coding/09-nlp/coreference-resolu.title: coreference-resolution
agentic-coding/09-nlp/coreference-resolu.content:
Coreference Resolution

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Finding which words refer to the same entity. Essential for understanding pronouns.
📋 Concrete Example
In Mary said she was tired, coreference resolution links she to Mary.
🔗 Analogy
Like a detective connecting nicknames, pronouns, and names to figure out who is who in a story.
Related Concepts

Named Entity Recognition
Semantics

agentic-coding/09-nlp/corpus.title: corpus
agentic-coding/09-nlp/corpus.content:
Corpus

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
A large collection of text used for training. The bigger and more diverse, the better the model learns.
📋 Concrete Example
Wikipedia, news articles, and books together form a corpus for training a language model.
🔗 Analogy
Like a library the model studies - the more books it reads, the more it knows.
Related Concepts

Dataset
Language Model
Pre-Training

agentic-coding/09-nlp/decoder.title: decoder
agentic-coding/09-nlp/decoder.content:
Decoder

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The part of a transformer that generates the output sequence one token at a time, using encoder context.
📋 Concrete Example
In translation, the decoder generates the English translation word by word, guided by the encoder output.
🔗 Analogy
Like a writer who takes the understanding and writes it out in a new language, one word at a time.
Related Concepts

Encoder
Transformer Architecture
Seq2Seq

agentic-coding/09-nlp/dependency-parsing.title: dependency-parsing
agentic-coding/09-nlp/dependency-parsing.content:
Dependency Parsing

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Analyzes the grammatical structure by finding relationships (head and dependent) between words.
📋 Concrete Example
In I eat rice, eat is the head, I is the subject dependent, and rice is the object dependent.
🔗 Analogy
Like drawing arrows between words to show who depends on whom in a sentence.
Related Concepts

Part of Speech Tagging
Syntax
Chunking

agentic-coding/09-nlp/distributed-repres.title: distributed-representation
agentic-coding/09-nlp/distributed-repres.content:
Distributed Representation

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Representing meaning as a pattern across many dimensions, not a single symbol. Embeddings do this.
📋 Concrete Example
The meaning of king is spread across 300 numbers, not stored in one slot labeled king.
🔗 Analogy
Like describing a color by its RGB values instead of just its name - more detailed and comparable.
Related Concepts

Embedding
Word2Vec
Vector

agentic-coding/09-nlp/embedding.title: embedding
agentic-coding/09-nlp/embedding.content:
Embedding

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Turns words or tokens into vectors of numbers so the computer can measure meaning and similarity.
📋 Concrete Example
The word happy might become [0.8, -0.1, 0.5, …]. Words with similar meaning get similar vectors.
🔗 Analogy
Like giving each word a fingerprint - similar words have similar prints, different words have different ones.
Related Concepts

Word2Vec
GloVe
Vector
Tokenization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/encoder.title: encoder
agentic-coding/09-nlp/encoder.content:
Encoder

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The part of a transformer that reads and understands the input, turning it into rich representations.
📋 Concrete Example
In translation, the encoder reads the Chinese sentence and produces a set of context vectors capturing its meaning.
🔗 Analogy
Like a reader who absorbs a story and forms a deep understanding of it in their mind.
Related Concepts

Decoder
Transformer Architecture
Self-Attention

agentic-coding/09-nlp/evaluation.title: evaluation
agentic-coding/09-nlp/evaluation.content:
Evaluation

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Measuring how good an NLP model is. Metrics include accuracy, F1, BLEU, and perplexity.
📋 Concrete Example
A translation model is evaluated with BLEU score comparing its output to human translations.
🔗 Analogy
Like a report card with different grades for different subjects - each metric measures a different aspect.
Related Concepts

Perplexity
BLEU Score
F1 Score

agentic-coding/09-nlp/f1-score.title: f1-score
agentic-coding/09-nlp/f1-score.content:
F1 Score

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The harmonic mean of precision and recall. Balances both into one number for classification tasks.
📋 Concrete Example
Precision 0.8, recall 0.6 -> F1 = 2 * (0.8*0.6)/(0.8+0.6) = 0.68. A single balanced score.
🔗 Analogy
Like a judge who weighs both how many correct answers you got (precision) and how many you missed (recall).
Related Concepts

Evaluation
Precision
Recall

agentic-coding/09-nlp/few-shot-learning.title: few-shot-learning
agentic-coding/09-nlp/few-shot-learning.content:
Few-Shot Learning

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Giving the model a few examples in the prompt to help it understand the task before asking it to perform.
📋 Concrete Example
Prompt: Here are 3 examples of formal vs informal text… Now classify this new sentence. The model follows the pattern.
🔗 Analogy
Like showing a new employee 3 example emails before asking them to write one - they learn the style quickly.
Related Concepts

Zero-Shot Learning
Prompt Engineering
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/fine-tuning.title: fine-tuning
agentic-coding/09-nlp/fine-tuning.content:
Fine-Tuning

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Training a pre-trained language model further on a specific dataset so it specializes in a task or domain.
📋 Concrete Example
Fine-tune GPT on Hong Kong legal documents to make a legal assistant chatbot.
🔗 Analogy
Like a general doctor taking extra training to become a heart specialist.
Related Concepts

Pre-Training
Transfer Learning
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/glove.title: glove
agentic-coding/09-nlp/glove.content:
GloVe

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Global Vectors: learns embeddings from word co-occurrence counts across the whole corpus.
📋 Concrete Example
GloVe looks at how often ice and steam appear near each other versus with other words, and places them accordingly.
🔗 Analogy
Like a popularity chart - words that hang out together in many books get similar scores.
Related Concepts

Word2Vec
Embedding
Vector

agentic-coding/09-nlp/gpt.title: gpt
agentic-coding/09-nlp/gpt.content:
GPT

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Generative Pre-trained Transformer. Autoregressive decoder that generates text token by token.
📋 Concrete Example
GPT reads your prompt and generates a response one token at a time, always looking left only.
🔗 Analogy
Like a storyteller who builds the tale word by word, each new word based on everything said so far.
Related Concepts

Causal Language Modeling
Decoder
Next Token Prediction
Transformer Architecture

agentic-coding/09-nlp/greedy-decoding.title: greedy-decoding
agentic-coding/09-nlp/greedy-decoding.content:
Greedy Decoding

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Always picks the most likely next token. Fast but can produce repetitive or suboptimal text.
📋 Concrete Example
The model always picks the highest-probability word. It might get stuck repeating the same phrase.
🔗 Analogy
Like always choosing the shortest path at each turn without looking ahead - you might hit a dead end.
Related Concepts

Beam Search
Sampling
Decoder

agentic-coding/09-nlp/hallucination.title: hallucination
agentic-coding/09-nlp/hallucination.content:
Hallucination

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
When a language model confidently states false information as if it were true. A major challenge in NLP.
📋 Concrete Example
A model might say Hong Kong was founded in 1843 (wrong, it was 1842) with full confidence.
🔗 Analogy
Like a student who makes up an answer on an exam and writes it confidently - sounds right, but is wrong.
Related Concepts

Language Model
Evaluation
GPT

agentic-coding/09-nlp/information-extrac.title: information-extraction
agentic-coding/09-nlp/information-extrac.content:
Information Extraction

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Pulling structured facts from unstructured text. NER, relation extraction, and event extraction.
📋 Concrete Example
From Apple was founded in 1976, extract: (Apple, founded, 1976). Turns text into a database.
🔗 Analogy
Like panning for gold - you sift through raw text to find the valuable structured nuggets.
Related Concepts

Named Entity Recognition
Relation Extraction

agentic-coding/09-nlp/language-model.title: language-model
agentic-coding/09-nlp/language-model.content:
Language Model

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
A model that assigns probabilities to sequences of text. Can predict the next word. The core of chatbots.
📋 Concrete Example
Given The sky is, a language model says blue is most likely (0.8), green less likely (0.05).
🔗 Analogy
Like a super-smart autocomplete on your phone that has read millions of books.
Related Concepts

N-Gram
Perplexity
Transformer Architecture
Next Token Prediction

agentic-coding/09-nlp/lemmatization.title: lemmatization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/lemmatization.content:
Lemmatization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Reduces words to their dictionary root form (lemma). Slower than stemming but more accurate.
📋 Concrete Example
Better becomes good. Running becomes run. Studies becomes study. All are real dictionary words.
🔗 Analogy
Like looking up a word in a dictionary to find its base form - accurate but takes a moment.
Related Concepts

Stemming
Preprocessing
Part of Speech Tagging

agentic-coding/09-nlp/machine-translatio.title: machine-translation
agentic-coding/09-nlp/machine-translatio.content:
Machine Translation

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Automatically translates text from one language to another. Google Translate and DeepL use this.
📋 Concrete Example
Input: Good morning. Output (Chinese): zao shang hao. The model learns mappings between languages.
🔗 Analogy
Like a bilingual friend who reads a Chinese text and tells you what it means in English.
Related Concepts

Seq2Seq
Encoder
Decoder
Attention

agentic-coding/09-nlp/masked-language-mo.title: masked-language-modeling
agentic-coding/09-nlp/masked-language-mo.content:
Masked Language Modeling

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Hides some tokens and asks the model to predict them. How BERT is trained.
📋 Concrete Example
The [MASK] sat on the mat. The model learns to predict cat from the surrounding context.
🔗 Analogy
Like a fill-in-the-blank quiz - the model learns language by guessing the hidden words.
Related Concepts

Language Model
BERT
Pre-Training

agentic-coding/09-nlp/multi-head-attenti.title: multi-head-attention
agentic-coding/09-nlp/multi-head-attenti.content:
Multi-Head Attention

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Runs several attention mechanisms in parallel, each focusing on different relationships, then combines results.
📋 Concrete Example
One head might focus on grammar, another on emotion, another on named entities - all at once.
🔗 Analogy
Like a team of detectives each looking at different clues (motive, alibi, evidence) and then pooling findings.
Related Concepts

Self-Attention
Transformer Architecture

agentic-coding/09-nlp/n-gram.title: n-gram
agentic-coding/09-nlp/n-gram.content:
N-Gram

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
A sequence of N consecutive tokens. Used to model local word patterns and predict the next word.
📋 Concrete Example
In I love AI so much, the bigrams (2-grams) are: I love, love AI, AI so, so much.
🔗 Analogy
Like looking at words two or three at a time, like reading through a magnifying glass that shows a small window.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Bag of Words
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/named-entity-recog.title: named-entity-recognition
agentic-coding/09-nlp/named-entity-recog.content:
Named Entity Recognition

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Finds and classifies names in text: people, places, organizations, dates, etc.
📋 Concrete Example
In Tim Cook visited Apple Park in Cupertino, NER finds: Tim Cook (PERSON), Apple Park (ORG), Cupertino (LOC).
🔗 Analogy
Like a highlighter that marks every proper noun and labels what kind of thing it is.
Related Concepts

Part of Speech Tagging
Information Extraction

agentic-coding/09-nlp/next-token-predict.title: next-token-prediction
agentic-coding/09-nlp/next-token-predict.content:
Next Token Prediction

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The fundamental task of autoregressive language models: guess the next token from the context so far.
📋 Concrete Example
Input: Hong Kong is famous for its. Model predicts: dim sum (0.3), skyline (0.2), harbor (0.15), …
🔗 Analogy
Like a guessing game where you predict the next word in a sentence your friend is saying.
Related Concepts

Causal Language Modeling
Language Model
GPT

agentic-coding/09-nlp/part-of-speech-tag.title: part-of-speech-tagging
agentic-coding/09-nlp/part-of-speech-tag.content:
Part of Speech Tagging

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Labels each word with its grammatical role: noun, verb, adjective, etc. Helps disambiguate meaning.
📋 Concrete Example
In I book a ticket, book is a verb. In I read a book, book is a noun. Same word, different tags.
🔗 Analogy
Like labeling each word in a sentence with a name tag saying I am a noun or I am a verb.
Related Concepts

Lemmatization
Named Entity Recognition
Syntax

agentic-coding/09-nlp/perplexity.title: perplexity
agentic-coding/09-nlp/perplexity.content:
Perplexity

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Measures how surprised a language model is by text. Lower perplexity means the model expected the text better.
📋 Concrete Example
A good language model has low perplexity on well-written English and high perplexity on random gibberish.
🔗 Analogy
Like a prediction game - if you guessed the text right, you are not perplexed; if it shocked you, perplexity is high.
Related Concepts

Language Model
Cross-Entropy
Evaluation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/positional-encodin.title: positional-encoding
agentic-coding/09-nlp/positional-encodin.content:
Positional Encoding

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Adds position information to tokens since attention has no built-in sense of order.
📋 Concrete Example
The model adds a position pattern to each token: token 1 gets pattern A, token 2 gets pattern B, etc.
🔗 Analogy
Like numbering the pages of a book - the text on each page needs a page number so you know the order.
Related Concepts

Transformer Architecture
Self-Attention
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/pre-training.title: pre-training
agentic-coding/09-nlp/pre-training.content:
Pre-Training

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Training a language model on a massive text corpus before any specific task. Gives general language understanding.
📋 Concrete Example
GPT is pre-trained on web text, books, and code. Then it is fine-tuned or prompted for specific tasks.
🔗 Analogy
Like a student doing broad reading for years before specializing in one subject at university.
Related Concepts

Fine-Tuning
Transfer Learning
Corpus

agentic-coding/09-nlp/precision.title: precision
agentic-coding/09-nlp/precision.content:
Precision

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Of the items the model predicted as positive, how many were actually positive. Measures quality of positive predictions.
📋 Concrete Example
Model predicts 10 emails are spam, 8 actually are. Precision = 8/10 = 0.8. 2 were false alarms.
🔗 Analogy
Like a fisherman checking his catch - of the 10 fish he kept, how many were the target species.
Related Concepts

F1 Score
Recall
Evaluation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/preprocessing.title: preprocessing
agentic-coding/09-nlp/preprocessing.content:
Preprocessing

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Cleaning and preparing raw text before feeding it to a model. Tokenization, lowercasing, removing noise.
📋 Concrete Example
Raw HTML gets tags stripped, text lowercased, tokenized, and stop words removed before analysis.
🔗 Analogy
Like washing and chopping vegetables before cooking - you prepare the ingredients first.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Stop Words
Stemming
Lemmatization

agentic-coding/09-nlp/prompt-engineering.title: prompt-engineering
agentic-coding/09-nlp/prompt-engineering.content:
Prompt Engineering

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Crafting the input prompt to get the best output from a language model. A key skill for using LLMs.
📋 Concrete Example
Adding Be specific and give 3 examples to a prompt can dramatically improve the response quality.
🔗 Analogy
Like asking a teacher the right question - a well-phrased question gets a much better answer.
Related Concepts

Language Model
GPT
Next Token Prediction

agentic-coding/09-nlp/question-answering.title: question-answering
agentic-coding/09-nlp/question-answering.content:
Question Answering

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Given a question and a context passage, the model finds or generates the answer.
📋 Concrete Example
Question: When was Hong Kong established? Context: Hong Kong was established in 1842. Answer: 1842.
🔗 Analogy
Like a student reading a passage then answering comprehension questions from it.
Related Concepts

Text Classification
Embedding
BERT

agentic-coding/09-nlp/recall.title: recall
agentic-coding/09-nlp/recall.content:
Recall

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Of all the actual positive items, how many the model found. Measures completeness.
📋 Concrete Example
There are 15 real spam emails. Model finds 8. Recall = 8/15 = 0.53. It missed 7.
🔗 Analogy
Like a search and rescue team - of all the lost hikers, how many did they find.
Related Concepts

F1 Score
Precision
Evaluation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/relation-extractio.title: relation-extraction
agentic-coding/09-nlp/relation-extractio.content:
Relation Extraction

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Finding relationships between entities in text. Builds knowledge graphs.
📋 Concrete Example
From Steve Jobs co-founded Apple, extract: (Steve Jobs, co-founded, Apple).
🔗 Analogy
Like connecting dots in a detective board - link people, companies, and events with strings.
Related Concepts

Named Entity Recognition
Information Extraction

agentic-coding/09-nlp/self-attention.title: self-attention
agentic-coding/09-nlp/self-attention.content:
Self-Attention

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Each token looks at all other tokens in the same sequence to understand its own meaning in context.
📋 Concrete Example
In The bark was loud, self-attention helps the model know bark means dog sound (not tree bark) by looking at loud.
🔗 Analogy
Like a group discussion where each person listens to everyone else to decide what they themselves mean.
Related Concepts

Attention Mechanism
Transformer Architecture
Multi-Head Attention

agentic-coding/09-nlp/semantics.title: semantics
agentic-coding/09-nlp/semantics.content:
Semantics

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The meaning of words and sentences. NLP aims to capture semantics, not just syntax.
📋 Concrete Example
The cat sat on the mat and The feline rested on the rug have different syntax but similar semantics.
🔗 Analogy
Like the difference between what a sentence says (syntax) and what it means (semantics).
Related Concepts

Syntax
Embedding
Word2Vec

agentic-coding/09-nlp/sentiment-analysis.title: sentiment-analysis
agentic-coding/09-nlp/sentiment-analysis.content:
Sentiment Analysis

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Determines if text is positive, negative, or neutral. Used for reviews, social media, and feedback.
📋 Concrete Example
This movie is great! is positive. The food was terrible and cold is negative.
🔗 Analogy
Like a mood ring for text - it tells you if the writer is happy, angry, or neutral.
Related Concepts

Classification
Text Classification
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/seq2seq.title: seq2seq
agentic-coding/09-nlp/seq2seq.content:
Seq2Seq

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Sequence-to-sequence models take an input sequence and produce an output sequence of different length.
📋 Concrete Example
Translation: input 5 Chinese words, output 7 English words. The lengths differ, and that is fine.
🔗 Analogy
Like a translator who reads a 3-line Chinese poem and writes a 4-line English version.
Related Concepts

Encoder
Decoder
Machine Translation
Attention

agentic-coding/09-nlp/stemming.title: stemming
agentic-coding/09-nlp/stemming.content:
Stemming

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Cuts off word endings to get a root form. Fast but crude - results may not be real words.
📋 Concrete Example
Running, runs, runner all stem to run. Studies might stem to studi (not a real word).
🔗 Analogy
Like pruning a tree with hedge clippers - quick and rough, not always pretty.
Related Concepts

Lemmatization
Preprocessing
Stop Words

agentic-coding/09-nlp/stop-words.title: stop-words
agentic-coding/09-nlp/stop-words.content:
Stop Words

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Common words like the, is, a that appear everywhere but carry little meaning. Often removed to save space.
📋 Concrete Example
Removing stop words from The cat sat on the mat gives cat sat mat. The core meaning stays.
🔗 Analogy
Like skimming a book and skipping filler words like um and uh to get to the real content.
Related Concepts

Bag of Words
TF-IDF
Preprocessing

agentic-coding/09-nlp/subword-tokenizati.title: subword-tokenization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/subword-tokenizati.content:
Subword Tokenization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Splits text into pieces smaller than words but bigger than characters. Handles rare and new words well.
📋 Concrete Example
Unbelievable might split into [Un, believe, able]. ChatGPT splits text into subword units like this.
🔗 Analogy
Like breaking a big Lego build into medium modules - flexible enough to build anything, efficient to store.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
BPE
WordPiece
Vocabulary

agentic-coding/09-nlp/summarization.title: summarization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/summarization.content:
Summarization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Producing a shorter version of a longer text while keeping the key points.
📋 Concrete Example
Input: 3-page news article. Output: 2-sentence summary capturing the headline event.
🔗 Analogy
Like writing a TL;DR at the top of a long email - the essence in a fraction of the words.
Related Concepts

Text Generation
Seq2Seq
Encoder

agentic-coding/09-nlp/syntax.title: syntax
agentic-coding/09-nlp/syntax.content:
Syntax

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The rules governing sentence structure and word order. Different from semantics (meaning).
📋 Concrete Example
Colorless green ideas sleep furiously is syntactically valid but semantically nonsensical.
🔗 Analogy
Like the grammar rules of a language - they tell you if a sentence is well-formed, not if it makes sense.
Related Concepts

Part of Speech Tagging
Dependency Parsing
Semantics

agentic-coding/09-nlp/temperature.title: temperature
agentic-coding/09-nlp/temperature.content:
Temperature

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Controls randomness in text generation. Low temperature is focused and safe; high temperature is creative and risky.
📋 Concrete Example
Temperature 0.1: model always picks likely words (boring but safe). Temperature 1.5: more random, sometimes creative, sometimes weird.
🔗 Analogy
Like a thermostat for creativity - low means stay calm and predictable, high means get wild and experimental.
Related Concepts

Sampling
Top-K Sampling
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/text-classificatio.title: text-classification
agentic-coding/09-nlp/text-classificatio.content:
Text Classification

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Assigning a category to a piece of text. Spam detection, sentiment analysis, and topic labeling are examples.
📋 Concrete Example
Email text -> model -> spam or not spam. News article -> model -> sports, politics, or tech.
🔗 Analogy
Like sorting mail into labeled folders - each piece of text goes into one category.
Related Concepts

Classification
Sentiment Analysis
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/text-generation.title: text-generation
agentic-coding/09-nlp/text-generation.content:
Text Generation

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Producing new text token by token. The core capability of chatbots and writing assistants.
📋 Concrete Example
Prompt: Write a poem about Hong Kong. The model generates: Victoria Harbour gleams at night …
🔗 Analogy
Like an author writing a story - each sentence builds on the last, creating something new.
Related Concepts

Language Model
Next Token Prediction
Decoder

agentic-coding/09-nlp/tf-idf.title: tf-idf
agentic-coding/09-nlp/tf-idf.content:
TF-IDF

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Term Frequency x Inverse Document Frequency. Highlights words that are important in a document but rare overall.
📋 Concrete Example
The appears in every document (low IDF, ignored). Quantum might appear in one physics paper (high TF-IDF, important).
🔗 Analogy
Like a word’s VIP score - frequent in this document but rare elsewhere means it is a keyword.
Related Concepts

Bag of Words
Vectorization
Information Retrieval

agentic-coding/09-nlp/tokenization.title: tokenization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/tokenization.content:
Tokenization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Computers cannot read whole sentences at once. We must split text into smaller pieces called tokens first.
📋 Concrete Example
The sentence I love AI splits into tokens: [I, love, AI]. Each token gets a number from the vocabulary.
🔗 Analogy
Like cutting a long sandwich into bite-size pieces before serving - easier to eat and count.
Related Concepts

Word Tokenization
Subword Tokenization
Character-Level Tokenization
Vocabulary

agentic-coding/09-nlp/top-k-sampling.title: top-k-sampling
agentic-coding/09-nlp/top-k-sampling.content:
Top-K Sampling

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Only samples from the K most likely next tokens, ignoring the long tail of unlikely ones.
📋 Concrete Example
Top-K = 40 means the model only considers the top 40 candidates and samples among them.
🔗 Analogy
Like a talent show where only the top 40 contestants get to perform - the rest are cut.
Related Concepts

Temperature
Sampling
Language Model

agentic-coding/09-nlp/top-p-sampling.title: top-p-sampling
agentic-coding/09-nlp/top-p-sampling.content:
Top-P Sampling

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches P (nucleus sampling).
📋 Concrete Example
Top-P = 0.9 means take tokens in order of probability until they add up to 90%, then sample from that set.
🔗 Analogy
Like packing a suitcase - take the most important items first until you reach 90% full, then pick randomly from the rest.
Related Concepts

Top-K Sampling
Temperature
Sampling

agentic-coding/09-nlp/transformer-archit.title: transformer-architecture
agentic-coding/09-nlp/transformer-archit.content:
Transformer Architecture

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The neural network design based entirely on attention, no recurrence. Powers all modern LLMs.
📋 Concrete Example
A transformer uses self-attention layers and feed-forward layers, processing all tokens at once in parallel.
🔗 Analogy
Like a round-table meeting where everyone speaks and listens at once, instead of a phone chain where messages pass one by one.
Related Concepts

Self-Attention
Positional Encoding
Encoder
Decoder

agentic-coding/09-nlp/vectorization.title: vectorization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/vectorization.content:
Vectorization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Converting text into numerical vectors that a model can process. Bag of words, TF-IDF, and embeddings all do this.
📋 Concrete Example
I love AI becomes [0.2, 0.8, 0.1, …] via embedding. Now the computer can do math on it.
🔗 Analogy
Like translating a poem into numbers - each word and its meaning become coordinates on a map.
Related Concepts

Bag of Words
TF-IDF
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/vocabulary.title: vocabulary
agentic-coding/09-nlp/vocabulary.content:
Vocabulary

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The set of all tokens a model knows. Each token maps to an ID number. Unknown tokens cause problems.
📋 Concrete Example
A vocabulary of 50000 subwords covers most English. A word outside it gets split into known subwords.
🔗 Analogy
Like a dictionary the model has memorized - if a word is not in it, the model has to describe it with smaller known pieces.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
BPE
Embedding

agentic-coding/09-nlp/word-tokenization.title: word-tokenization
agentic-coding/09-nlp/word-tokenization.content:
Word Tokenization

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Splitting text by spaces and punctuation into individual words. The simplest tokenization method.
📋 Concrete Example
Hello, world! becomes [Hello, ,, world, !]. Punctuation marks are often separate tokens.
🔗 Analogy
Like tearing a sentence into individual word cards, one word per card.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Subword Tokenization
Vocabulary

agentic-coding/09-nlp/word2vec.title: word2vec
agentic-coding/09-nlp/word2vec.content:
Word2Vec

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Learns word embeddings by predicting words from context. Similar words end up with similar vectors.
📋 Concrete Example
After training, vector(king) - vector(man) + vector(woman) is close to vector(queen). Famous word analogy.
🔗 Analogy
Like a GPS for meaning - words that mean similar things end up close together on the map.
Related Concepts

Embedding
GloVe
Vector
Distributed Representation

agentic-coding/09-nlp/wordpiece.title: wordpiece
agentic-coding/09-nlp/wordpiece.content:
WordPiece

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
Like BPE but builds vocabulary for language understanding (BERT). Uses  prefix for non-starting pieces.
📋 Concrete Example
Playing splits to [Play, ##ing]. The double-hash marks that ing attaches to the previous piece.
🔗 Analogy
Like labeling puzzle pieces - the piece with  is a connector that must follow another piece.
Related Concepts

BPE
Subword Tokenization
Vocabulary

agentic-coding/09-nlp/zero-shot-learning.title: zero-shot-learning
agentic-coding/09-nlp/zero-shot-learning.content:
Zero-Shot Learning

Domain: NLP Fundamentals

🎯 Motivation
The model performs a task it has never been explicitly trained on, using only its general knowledge and the prompt.
📋 Concrete Example
Ask a model to classify sentiment of Cantonese text even if it was never trained on a sentiment task in Cantonese.
🔗 Analogy
Like a student tackling a brand new question type on an exam using general reasoning, never having practiced it.
Related Concepts

Few-Shot Learning
Prompt Engineering
Language Model
