agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/clusteri.title: clustering
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/clusteri.content:
Clustering

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Grouping similar items without labels. An unsupervised learning technique.
📋 Concrete Example
Clustering: 1000 news articles -> 5 groups (sports, politics, tech, entertainment, health). The model found these groups without being told the categories.
🔗 Analogy
Sorting laundry - you naturally separate whites, colors, and delicates. No labels needed - you see similarity. Clustering groups items by similarity.
Related Concepts

Unsupervised Learning
Similarity Search
K-Means

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/corpus.title: corpus
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/corpus.content:
Corpus

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A large collection of text used for training. Can include books, articles, websites, code.
📋 Concrete Example
Corpus: 5 million books, 20 million articles, 100 million web pages, 10 million code files. The model learns language patterns from this massive text collection.
🔗 Analogy
A library’s entire collection - millions of books on every topic. A corpus is the model’s library, the text it learns from.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Pre-training
Dataset

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/curricul.title: curriculum-learning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/curricul.content:
Curriculum Learning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Training the model on easy examples first, then gradually harder ones. Like a school curriculum.
📋 Concrete Example
Curriculum: 1) Easy examples (simple sentences). 2) Medium (paragraphs). 3) Hard (complex essays). The model builds up skills gradually, like a student.
🔗 Analogy
A math curriculum: addition -> subtraction -> multiplication -> division -> algebra. Start easy, get harder. Curriculum learning trains AI step by step.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Learning Rate
Machine Learning

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ann.title: data-annotation-guideline
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ann.content:
Data Annotation Guideline

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Rules for how to label data. Consistent guidelines produce consistent, high-quality labels.
📋 Concrete Example
Guideline: ‘Label as positive only if the text expresses clear happiness. Uncertain = neutral. Sarcasm = negative.’ All annotators follow the same rules.
🔗 Analogy
A grading rubric for teachers - ‘5 = excellent, 3 = average, 1 = poor. Specific criteria for each score.’ Annotation guidelines are rubrics for data labeling.
Related Concepts

Annotation
Labeling
Data Quality

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-aug.title: data-augmentation
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-aug.content:
Data Augmentation

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Creating more training data by modifying existing data: flipping, rotating, paraphrasing. Increases dataset size and diversity.
📋 Concrete Example
Augmentation: 1 photo of a cat -> flip, rotate, crop, adjust brightness = 10 photos. Dataset grows from 1K to 10K images. More diverse training data.
🔗 Analogy
A chef creating variations of a dish - same ingredients, different presentations. Data augmentation creates variations of data for more robust training.
Related Concepts

Data Preprocessing
Training Data
Synthetic Data

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-bal.title: data-balance
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-bal.content:
Data Balance

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Having equal or proportional representation across categories. Imbalanced data causes biased models.
📋 Concrete Example
Balance: 50% cat images, 50% dog images. Balanced. vs 90% cat, 10% dog. Imbalanced - model will be biased toward cats. Balance ensures fair training.
🔗 Analogy
A balanced diet - equal portions of protein, vegetables, and carbs. Data balance ensures the model learns all categories equally.
Related Concepts

Data Distribution
Bias in AI
Class Weight

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-cle.title: data-cleaning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-cle.content:
Data Cleaning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Fixing errors in data: removing duplicates, fixing labels, handling missing values, correcting formatting.
📋 Concrete Example
Cleaning: remove 500 duplicate entries, fix 200 mislabeled items, fill 50 missing values, standardize date formats. Clean data = better training.
🔗 Analogy
Washing vegetables before cooking - you remove dirt and bad spots. Data cleaning removes errors and inconsistencies before training.
Related Concepts

Data Quality
Data Preprocessing
Outlier Removal

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ded.title: data-deduplication
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ded.content:
Data Deduplication

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Removing duplicate entries from the dataset. Duplicates cause the model to over-represent repeated patterns.
📋 Concrete Example
Deduplication: 1M articles, find 50K exact duplicates and 20K near-duplicates. Remove them. 930K unique articles remain. Better training.
🔗 Analogy
Removing duplicate photos from your camera roll - you keep one copy of each photo. Deduplication keeps one copy of each data example.
Related Concepts

Data Cleaning
Data Quality
Training Data

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-dis.title: data-distribution
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-dis.content:
Data Distribution

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
How data is spread across categories, values, or time. Understanding distribution prevents bias.
📋 Concrete Example
Distribution: 80% of training data is about Western culture, 20% rest of world. The model will be biased toward Western knowledge. Distribution matters.
🔗 Analogy
A classroom demographic - 30 boys and 5 girls. The class is skewed. Data distribution shows how data is spread, revealing potential biases.
Related Concepts

Bias in AI
Training Data
Data Balance

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-lea.title: data-leakage
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-lea.content:
Data Leakage

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
When test data accidentally leaks into training data. Causes inflated scores that do not hold in real use.
📋 Concrete Example
Leakage: the same article appears in both train and test sets. The model memorizes it. Test score: 95%. Real-world score: 70%. The leakage caused false confidence.
🔗 Analogy
A student accidentally seeing the exam before the test - they score 95% but do not really know the material. Data leakage gives false high scores.
Related Concepts

Train-Test Split
Overfitting
Model Evaluation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pip.title: data-pipeline
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pip.content:
Data Pipeline

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
The end-to-end process: collect -> clean -> preprocess -> augment -> split -> train -> evaluate. Automated for efficiency.
📋 Concrete Example
Pipeline: 1) Scrape 1M articles. 2) Clean (remove duplicates, fix encoding). 3) Tokenize. 4) Split (80/10/10). 5) Train model. 6) Evaluate. Automated end-to-end.
🔗 Analogy
A water treatment pipeline - water flows through: collection -> filtration -> chemical treatment -> testing -> distribution. Each stage processes the water. A data pipeline processes data.
Related Concepts

Data Preprocessing
Training Data
Automation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pre.title: data-preprocessing
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pre.content:
Data Preprocessing

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Transforming raw data into a format suitable for training: tokenizing, normalizing, augmenting, splitting.
📋 Concrete Example
Preprocessing: raw text -> tokenize -> lowercase -> remove punctuation -> pad sequences -> split into train/test. Raw data becomes training-ready.
🔗 Analogy
Prepping ingredients before cooking - wash, peel, chop, measure. Raw ingredients become cooking-ready. Data preprocessing makes raw data training-ready.
Related Concepts

Data Cleaning
Tokenization
Normalization

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pro.title: data-provenance-in-training
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-pro.content:
Data Provenance in Training

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Tracking where every piece of training data came from: source, date, modifications, license. Essential for compliance.
📋 Concrete Example
Provenance: ‘Article 1234: source: BBC News, date: 2024-03-15, original, license: CC-BY, no modifications.’ Full traceability for every training example.
🔗 Analogy
A diamond’s certificate - mine of origin, cut date, carat weight, chain of ownership. Data provenance is the certificate for each training example.
Related Concepts

Data Collection
Data Versioning
Audit Trail

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-qua.title: data-quality
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-qua.content:
Data Quality

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
How good the data is: accurate, complete, diverse, relevant, unbiased. Better data = better models.
📋 Concrete Example
Quality check: 95% accurate labels, 0% duplicates, diverse topics, no bias, relevant to task. High quality. vs 60% accurate labels, 20% duplicates, biased. Low quality.
🔗 Analogy
Ingredients for cooking - fresh, high-quality ingredients make better dishes. High-quality data makes better models. Data quality is the freshness of the ingredients.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Data Cleaning
Labeling

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-sam.title: data-sampling
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-sam.content:
Data Sampling

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Selecting a subset of data for training or evaluation. Different sampling strategies for different needs.
📋 Concrete Example
Sampling: from 1M articles, randomly select 100K for training. Or stratified sample: ensure equal representation from each category. Strategy matters.
🔗 Analogy
Taking a spoonful of soup to taste - you sample a small part to represent the whole. Data sampling selects representative subsets for training.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Data Distribution
Stratified Sampling

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ver.title: data-versioning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/data-ver.content:
Data Versioning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Tracking changes to datasets over time, like git for data. Essential for reproducibility.
📋 Concrete Example
Dataset v1: 10K examples. v2: 15K examples (added 5K). v3: 14K examples (removed 1K bad ones). Versioning tracks what changed and when.
🔗 Analogy
Saving drafts of an essay - v1, v2, v3. You can see what changed. Data versioning tracks dataset changes like draft versions.
Related Concepts

Data Pipeline
Reproducibility
Version Control

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/dataset.title: dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/dataset.content:
Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A structured collection of data used for training, testing, or evaluation. Can be text, images, audio, or mixed.
📋 Concrete Example
ImageNet: 1.4M labeled images across 1000 categories. Used to train image recognition models. The dataset defines what the model can recognize.
🔗 Analogy
A question bank for an exam - 10,000 questions organized by topic and difficulty. The dataset is the question bank for model training.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Data Collection
Labeling

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/embeddin.title: embedding-dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/embeddin.content:
Embedding Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A dataset of pre-computed embeddings (vector representations). Used for similarity search, clustering, and retrieval.
📋 Concrete Example
Embedding dataset: 1M sentences, each as a 768-dimension vector. Find similar sentences by computing vector distance. Fast similarity search.
🔗 Analogy
A library catalog with GPS coordinates - each book has a location. Find nearby books by distance. An embedding dataset has vectors for similarity search.
Related Concepts

Embedding
Vector Database
Similarity Search

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/few-shot.title: few-shot-dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/few-shot.content:
Few-Shot Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A dataset with only a few examples per category (3-10). Tests the model’s ability to learn from few examples.
📋 Concrete Example
Few-shot: 5 examples of each animal type. Can the model recognize new animals after seeing just 5 examples? Few-shot learning tests this.
🔗 Analogy
Learning a new card game - someone shows you 5 examples, then you play. Few-shot datasets test if the model can learn from just a few examples.
Related Concepts

Few-Shot Learning
Training Data
Dataset

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/instruct.title: instruction-dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/instruct.content:
Instruction Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A dataset of instruction-response pairs. Used to teach models to follow instructions (instruction tuning).
📋 Concrete Example
Instruction dataset: {instruction: ‘Summarize this article’, input: ‘Article text…’, output: Summary...}. 100K such pairs. Model learns to follow instructions.
🔗 Analogy
A workbook with example problems and solutions - the student learns the pattern. An instruction dataset teaches the model to follow instructions.
Related Concepts

Instruction Tuning
Training Data
Dataset

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/inter-an.title: inter-annotator-agreement
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/inter-an.content:
Inter-Annotator Agreement

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
How often different annotators agree on labels. High agreement = clear guidelines and consistent labels.
📋 Concrete Example
5 annotators label 1000 texts. Agreement: 92%. High - labels are consistent. If agreement was 60%, guidelines need improvement.
🔗 Analogy
Judges at a diving competition - if all judges give similar scores (high agreement), the scoring is consistent. Inter-annotator agreement measures labeling consistency.
Related Concepts

Annotation
Labeling
Data Quality

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/labeling.title: labeling
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/labeling.content:
Labeling

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Adding correct answers to training examples. Supervised learning needs labeled data.
📋 Concrete Example
Labeling: image of a cat -> label: cat. Image of a dog -> label: dog. 10,000 images labeled = dataset ready for supervised training.
🔗 Analogy
A teacher marking answer keys on practice exams - each question gets the correct answer. Labeling marks the correct answer for each training example.
Related Concepts

Dataset
Supervised Learning
Annotation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/multimod.title: multimodal-dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/multimod.content:
Multimodal Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A dataset containing multiple data types: text + images, text + audio, text + video. For training multimodal models.
📋 Concrete Example
Multimodal: 100K items, each with: an image, a caption, and a question-answer pair. The model learns to understand relationships between images and text.
🔗 Analogy
A textbook with text and pictures - you learn from both together. A multimodal dataset has multiple data types for the model to learn from.
Related Concepts

Multimodal AI
Dataset
Data Preprocessing

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/outlier-.title: outlier-detection
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/outlier-.content:
Outlier Detection

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Identifying data points that are very different from the rest. Can be done statistically or with ML.
📋 Concrete Example
Detection: z-score > 3 = outlier. One article has 10,000 words (average: 500). z-score: 8.5. Outlier! Flag it for review or removal.
🔗 Analogy
A teacher noticing one student scored 0 while others scored 80-100. The 0 is an outlier. Outlier detection finds these anomalies automatically.
Related Concepts

Outlier Removal
Data Cleaning
Anomaly Detection

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/outlier-.title: outlier-removal
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/outlier-.content:
Outlier Removal

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Removing data points that are very different from the rest. Outliers can mislead the model.
📋 Concrete Example
Outlier: one article is 500 pages (average is 2 pages). Remove it - it would skew training. Outlier removal keeps the dataset consistent.
🔗 Analogy
Removing a score of 0 from a test where everyone else scored 80-100 - the 0 is an outlier that would skew the average. Outlier removal keeps data consistent.
Related Concepts

Data Cleaning
Data Quality
Outlier Detection

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/preferen.title: preference-dataset
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/preferen.content:
Preference Dataset

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A dataset of preferred vs non-preferred responses. Used for RLHF to align models with human preferences.
📋 Concrete Example
Preference data: {prompt: ‘What is Python?’, chosen: ‘Python is a programming language…’, rejected: ‘idk lol’}. Model learns to prefer good responses.
🔗 Analogy
A teacher’s feedback: ‘This essay is better than that one.’ The student learns what makes a good essay. Preference datasets teach models what humans prefer.
Related Concepts

RLHF
Preference Ranking
Reward Model

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/random-s.title: random-seed
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/random-s.content:
Random Seed

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A number that initializes random processes. Same seed = same random sequence = same results. Essential for reproducibility.
📋 Concrete Example
Seed = 42: model gets 85.2% accuracy. Seed = 123: model gets 84.8%. Same seed always gives the same result. Fix the seed for reproducibility.
🔗 Analogy
The starting position in a board game - same starting position = same game possibilities. A random seed sets the starting position for AI training.
Related Concepts

Reproducibility
Training Data
Determinism

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/reinforc.title: reinforcement-learning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/reinforc.content:
Reinforcement Learning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Learning by trial and error. The model gets rewards for good actions and penalties for bad ones.
📋 Concrete Example
A game-playing AI: it tries moves, gets points (rewards) or loses points (penalties). Over millions of games, it learns the best strategies. AlphaGo learned this way.
🔗 Analogy
Training a dog - correct behavior gets a treat (reward), bad behavior gets nothing (penalty). The dog learns through trial and error. RL trains AI the same way.
Related Concepts

Machine Learning
Reward Model
Exploration vs Exploitation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/reproduc.title: reproducibility
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/reproduc.content:
Reproducibility

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Can someone else get the same results with the same data and code? Essential for scientific credibility.
📋 Concrete Example
Reproducibility: ‘Here is the data (v3), code (v2.1), and random seed (42). Anyone can re-run and get 85.2% accuracy.’ Without reproducibility, results cannot be trusted.
🔗 Analogy
A science experiment - you write the procedure so others can replicate it and get the same result. Reproducibility means others can reproduce your AI results.
Related Concepts

Data Versioning
Random Seed
Model Evaluation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/stratifi.title: stratified-sampling
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/stratifi.content:
Stratified Sampling

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Sampling that maintains the proportion of each category. Ensures balanced representation.
📋 Concrete Example
Stratified: original data is 60% sports, 40% news. Sample 1000: 600 sports, 400 news. Proportions maintained. No category is underrepresented.
🔗 Analogy
A school survey that samples proportionally from each grade - 30% F1, 25% F2, 25% F3, 20% F4. Each grade is fairly represented.
Related Concepts

Data Sampling
Data Balance
Data Distribution

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/supervis.title: supervised-learning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/supervis.content:
Supervised Learning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Learning from labeled examples: input -> correct output. The model learns to map inputs to outputs.
📋 Concrete Example
Training: 10,000 emails labeled spam or ‘not spam.’ Model learns patterns. New email -> model predicts spam or ‘not spam.’ Supervised = with labeled examples.
🔗 Analogy
A student learning with answer keys - they see questions and correct answers, then learn to solve new questions. Supervised learning uses labeled examples.
Related Concepts

Labeling
Machine Learning
Unsupervised Learning

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/syntheti.title: synthetic-data
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/syntheti.content:
Synthetic Data

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Artificially generated data that mimics real data. Used when real data is scarce, private, or expensive.
📋 Concrete Example
Need 100K medical records but privacy laws prevent using real ones. Generate synthetic records with similar patterns. No real patient data exposed. Training proceeds.
🔗 Analogy
A flight simulator - synthetic (fake) scenarios that mimic real flying. Pilots train without real risk. Synthetic data trains models without real data limitations.
Related Concepts

Data Augmentation
Training Data
Data Privacy

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/test-set.title: test-set
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/test-set.content:
Test Set

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Data the model has never seen, used only for final evaluation. Provides an honest performance estimate.
📋 Concrete Example
Test set: 2,000 new examples. Model scores 85%. This is the honest estimate of real-world performance. The model never trained on or tuned with this data.
🔗 Analogy
The real HKDSE exam - questions the student has never seen. It provides an honest measure of their ability. The test set is the real exam for the model.
Related Concepts

Train-Test Split
Validation Set
Generalization

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/tokeniza.title: tokenization-data
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/tokeniza.content:
Tokenization Data

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Data about how text is split into tokens. Tokenization quality affects model performance.
📋 Concrete Example
Tokenization: unbelievable -> [un, believ, able] (subword). The model learns these subword units. Good tokenization = better understanding.
🔗 Analogy
Breaking a word into syllables - un-be-liev-a-ble. Each syllable is a unit. Tokenization breaks text into model-understandable units.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Data Preprocessing
Vocabulary

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/train-te.title: train-test-split
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/train-te.content:
Train-Test Split

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Dividing data into training set (80%) and test set (20%). Train on one, test on the other. Prevents evaluating on training data.
📋 Concrete Example
Split: 10,000 examples. Train: 8,000 (learn from these). Test: 2,000 (evaluate on these). The model never sees test data during training. Honest evaluation.
🔗 Analogy
A teacher’s practice exam vs real exam - practice (training) questions are studied, real (test) questions are new. The split ensures honest evaluation.
Related Concepts

Training Data
Validation Set
Model Evaluation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/training.title: training-data
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/training.content:
Training Data

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
The examples a model learns from. Quality and quantity of training data directly determine model performance.
📋 Concrete Example
GPT-4 was trained on millions of documents: books, articles, code, conversations. The diversity and quality of this data shaped its capabilities.
🔗 Analogy
A student’s textbooks and lecture notes - the quality of these learning materials directly determines how well they understand the subject. Training data is the model’s textbook.
Related Concepts

Dataset
Data Quality
Pre-training

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/unsuperv.title: unsupervised-learning
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/unsuperv.content:
Unsupervised Learning

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
Finding patterns in data without labels. The model discovers structure on its own.
📋 Concrete Example
10,000 customer profiles, no labels. Model finds: 3 groups (young spenders, budget families, luxury buyers). Clustering - unsupervised pattern discovery.
🔗 Analogy
Sorting a mixed bag of Lego bricks by color and shape - no instructions (labels), you just find natural groups. Unsupervised learning finds patterns without labels.
Related Concepts

Clustering
Machine Learning
Supervised Learning

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/validati.title: validation-set
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/validati.content:
Validation Set

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
A third data split used during training to tune hyperparameters. Separate from both training and test sets.
📋 Concrete Example
Split: 70% train, 15% validation, 15% test. Validation set is used to tune learning rate, model size, etc. Test set is used only for final evaluation.
🔗 Analogy
A dress rehearsal before opening night - rehearsal (train), dress rehearsal (validation, tune things), opening night (test, final evaluation).
Related Concepts

Train-Test Split
Hyperparameter Tuning
Model Evaluation

agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/vocabula.title: vocabulary
agentic-coding/20-data-datasets/vocabula.content:
Vocabulary

Domain: Data & Datasets

🎯 Motivation
The set of all tokens a model knows. Larger vocabulary = more tokens = finer text representation.
📋 Concrete Example
Vocabulary: 50,000 tokens. cat, dog, un, believ, able are all in the vocabulary. The model can represent any text using these 50K tokens.
🔗 Analogy
A student’s vocabulary - the words they know. A larger vocabulary means they can express more ideas. A model’s vocabulary works the same way.
Related Concepts

Tokenization
Embedding
Language Model

agentic-coding/21-mlops/ab-testing.title: ab-testing
agentic-coding/21-mlops/ab-testing.content:
A/B Testing

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Comparing two model versions: A (current) and B (new). Route some traffic to B, compare results, keep the winner.
📋 Concrete Example
A/B test: 90% of users get model A, 10% get model B. B has 3% higher satisfaction. Promote B to 100%. Data-driven decisions.
🔗 Analogy
A taste test at a restaurant - 90% of customers get the old recipe, 10% get the new one. If the new one is preferred, switch entirely.

Model Evaluation
Version Comparison
Experiment

agentic-coding/21-mlops/alerting.title: alerting
agentic-coding/21-mlops/alerting.content:
Alerting

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Automatic notifications when model performance degrades, errors spike, or anomalies are detected.
📋 Concrete Example
Alert: ‘Model accuracy dropped from 88% to 75% in the last hour. Investigate.’ The team gets a Slack message and investigates immediately.
🔗 Analogy
A smoke alarm - it detects smoke and alerts you immediately. Alerting notifies the team when model performance degrades.
Related Concepts

Model Monitoring
Drift Detection
Error Recovery

agentic-coding/21-mlops/auto-scaling.title: auto-scaling
agentic-coding/21-mlops/auto-scaling.content:
Auto-Scaling

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Automatically adding or removing model instances based on demand. Scale up when busy, scale down when quiet.
📋 Concrete Example
Auto-scaling: peak hours (9am-5pm) -> 20 instances. Off-peak (2am) -> 2 instances. Saves money while maintaining performance. Automatic.
🔗 Analogy
A store opening more registers when busy - lunch rush: 5 registers open. Quiet afternoon: 1 register. Auto-scaling opens and closes model instances based on demand.
Related Concepts

Scalability
Load Balancing
Cost Optimization

agentic-coding/21-mlops/batching.title: batching
agentic-coding/21-mlops/batching.content:
Batching

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Processing multiple requests together instead of one at a time. Much more efficient for GPUs.
📋 Concrete Example
Batching: 32 requests arrive. Process all 32 in one forward pass (batch size 32). 10x faster than processing one at a time. GPU optimized for batches.
🔗 Analogy
A bus vs individual cars - a bus carries 40 people at once (batch). More efficient than 40 individual cars. Batching carries multiple requests at once.
Related Concepts

Inference
Throughput
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/caching.title: caching
agentic-coding/21-mlops/caching.content:
Caching

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Storing recent results so identical requests do not need to be re-processed. Much faster for repeated queries.
📋 Concrete Example
Cache: user asks ‘What is Python?’ Model answers. Another user asks the same. Return cached answer instantly. No re-processing needed.
🔗 Analogy
A shortcut on your desk - the document you use most often is on your desk (cache), not in the filing cabinet. Instant access. Caching stores frequent results.
Related Concepts

Inference
Latency
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/canary-deploymen.title: canary-deployment
agentic-coding/21-mlops/canary-deploymen.content:
Canary Deployment

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Releasing a new model to a small percentage of users first. If no problems, gradually increase to 100%.
📋 Concrete Example
Canary: new model to 5% of users. Monitor for 24 hours: no errors, good feedback. Increase to 25%, then 50%, then 100%. Safe rollout.
🔗 Analogy
Testing a new dish at a restaurant - offer it as a special to a few customers first. If they like it, put it on the full menu. Canary deployment tests new models safely.
Related Concepts

Model Deployment
CI-CD
Rollback

agentic-coding/21-mlops/ci-cd.title: ci-cd
agentic-coding/21-mlops/ci-cd.content:
CI-CD

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment - automatically building, testing, and deploying models when code changes.
📋 Concrete Example
CI-CD pipeline: code change -> run tests -> build model -> evaluate -> deploy to staging -> canary test -> deploy to production. All automated.
🔗 Analogy
A factory assembly line - raw materials go in, quality checks happen automatically, finished products come out. CI-CD is the assembly line for AI models.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Continuous Integration
Continuous Deployment

agentic-coding/21-mlops/continuous-deplo.title: continuous-deployment
agentic-coding/21-mlops/continuous-deplo.content:
Continuous Deployment

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Automatically deploying code that passes CI. No manual intervention needed.
📋 Concrete Example
CD: code passes all tests -> automatically deployed to staging -> canary test (10% of traffic) -> if good, deployed to all users. Fully automated.
🔗 Analogy
An escalator - you step on and it automatically takes you to the next floor. No buttons, no waiting. Continuous deployment automatically moves code to production.
Related Concepts

CI-CD
Continuous Integration
Model Deployment

agentic-coding/21-mlops/continuous-integ.title: continuous-integration
agentic-coding/21-mlops/continuous-integ.content:
Continuous Integration

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Automatically testing code changes. Every commit triggers tests. Prevents broken code from merging.
📋 Concrete Example
CI: developer pushes code. Automatically: unit tests run, integration tests run, model tests run. All pass -> merge. Any fail -> reject. Automated quality gate.
🔗 Analogy
A checkpoint on a hiking trail - at each checkpoint, you check your gear and health before continuing. CI checks code at every commit before it merges.
Related Concepts

CI-CD
Testing
Automation

agentic-coding/21-mlops/cost-optimizatio.title: cost-optimization
agentic-coding/21-mlops/cost-optimizatio.content:
Cost Optimization

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Minimizing the cost of running models: right-sizing instances, using spot instances, optimizing batch sizes.
📋 Concrete Example
Optimization: 1) Use smaller model for simple queries. 2) Batch requests. 3) Use spot instances (cheaper). 4) Auto-scale. Cost reduced by 60%.
🔗 Analogy
Budgeting for a household - use cheaper brands, buy in bulk, turn off lights when not needed. Cost optimization reduces AI operating costs similarly.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Auto-Scaling
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/drift-detection.title: drift-detection
agentic-coding/21-mlops/drift-detection.content:
Drift Detection

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Detecting when real-world data changes from training data. The model performs worse because the world changed.
📋 Concrete Example
Drift: model trained on 2023 data. In 2025, slang has changed. Model does not understand new slang. Data drift detected. Retrain with new data.
🔗 Analogy
A map becoming outdated - new roads are built, old ones closed. The map (model) no longer matches reality (drift). Retrain with new data.
Related Concepts

Model Monitoring
Data Distribution
Retraining

agentic-coding/21-mlops/edge-deployment.title: edge-deployment
agentic-coding/21-mlops/edge-deployment.content:
Edge Deployment

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Running models on local devices (phones, IoT) instead of cloud servers. Lower latency, better privacy.
📋 Concrete Example
Edge: model runs on the phone. No data sent to cloud. Instant response. Private. But model must be small (compressed). Trade-off: size vs capability.
🔗 Analogy
A pocket dictionary vs a library - the dictionary (edge) is small and instant. The library (cloud) is comprehensive but requires travel. Edge deployment is the pocket dictionary.
Related Concepts

Model Deployment
Model Compression
Latency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/experiment-track.title: experiment-tracking
agentic-coding/21-mlops/experiment-track.content:
Experiment Tracking

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Logging every training experiment: hyperparameters, data version, model architecture, results. For reproducibility.
📋 Concrete Example
Experiment log: {exp_42: lr=0.001, batch=32, data_v3, accuracy=88%}. {exp_43: lr=0.002, batch=64, data_v3, accuracy=85%}. All tracked for comparison.
🔗 Analogy
A scientist’s lab notebook - every experiment is logged: conditions, procedure, results. Experiment tracking is the lab notebook for AI experiments.
Related Concepts

Reproducibility
Model Registry
Hyperparameter Tuning

agentic-coding/21-mlops/feature-store.title: feature-store
agentic-coding/21-mlops/feature-store.content:
Feature Store

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
A centralized store for features (input variables). Ensures consistency between training and serving.
📋 Concrete Example
Feature store: user_age, purchase_history, click_rate. Training uses these features. Serving uses the same features. Consistent.
🔗 Analogy
A pantry in a restaurant - ingredients are stored centrally. Both the prep kitchen (training) and the cooking line (serving) use the same pantry. A feature store ensures consistency.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Data Pipeline
Consistency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/federated-learni.title: federated-learning
agentic-coding/21-mlops/federated-learni.content:
Federated Learning

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Training models across multiple devices without collecting data centrally. Privacy-preserving.
📋 Concrete Example
Federated: 1000 phones each train on local data. Only model updates (not data) are sent to server. Server combines updates. Privacy preserved.
🔗 Analogy
A study group where each student studies at home, then shares what they learned (not their notes). The group combines insights. Federated learning trains across devices without sharing data.
Related Concepts

Data Privacy
Training Data
Edge Deployment

agentic-coding/21-mlops/gpu-utilization.title: gpu-utilization
agentic-coding/21-mlops/gpu-utilization.content:
GPU Utilization

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Maximizing GPU usage during training and inference. Idle GPUs waste money; fully utilized GPUs are efficient.
📋 Concrete Example
Utilization: 95% GPU during training (good). 30% GPU during inference (bad - batch more). Monitor and optimize to keep GPUs busy.
🔗 Analogy
A factory running at 95% capacity - machines are busy, efficient. At 30%, machines sit idle, wasting money. GPU utilization keeps GPUs busy.
Related Concepts

Cost Optimization
Batching
Inference

agentic-coding/21-mlops/grid-search.title: grid-search
agentic-coding/21-mlops/grid-search.content:
Grid Search

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Trying all combinations of hyperparameters systematically. Thorough but slow.
📋 Concrete Example
Grid: lr in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1} x batch in {32, 64, 128} = 9 combinations. Try all 9. Pick the best. Thorough but takes 9x training time.
🔗 Analogy
Trying every combination at a buffet - sample every dish x every sauce. Thorough but takes a long time. Grid search tries every hyperparameter combination.
Related Concepts

Hyperparameter Tuning
Experiment Tracking
Random Search

agentic-coding/21-mlops/hyperparameter-t.title: hyperparameter-tuning
agentic-coding/21-mlops/hyperparameter-t.content:
Hyperparameter Tuning

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Finding the best hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, model size) through systematic search.
📋 Concrete Example
Tuning: try lr=0.001 (88%), lr=0.01 (85%), lr=0.0001 (82%). Best: lr=0.001. Systematic search finds optimal settings.
🔗 Analogy
Tuning a guitar - try different string tensions until it sounds right. Hyperparameter tuning tries different settings until the model performs best.
Related Concepts

Experiment Tracking
Learning Rate
Grid Search

agentic-coding/21-mlops/inference.title: inference
agentic-coding/21-mlops/inference.content:
Inference

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Using a trained model to make predictions. The model is running, not training.
📋 Concrete Example
Inference: user sends ‘translate this text.’ Model processes it and returns the translation. This is inference - using the model, not training it.
🔗 Analogy
A chef cooking from a recipe - the recipe (model) is already written. Cooking (inference) uses it to produce dishes (predictions).
Related Concepts

Model Serving
Latency
Throughput

agentic-coding/21-mlops/knowledge-distil.title: knowledge-distillation
agentic-coding/21-mlops/knowledge-distil.content:
Knowledge Distillation

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
A small student model learns from a large teacher model. Student is small but inherits teacher’s knowledge.
📋 Concrete Example
Teacher: 175B parameters, 92% accuracy. Student: 7B parameters, 85% accuracy. Student learned from teacher’s outputs. Small, fast, decent accuracy.
🔗 Analogy
A master teaching an apprentice - the master (teacher) has deep knowledge. The apprentice (student) learns from the master. Smaller but capable.
Related Concepts

Model Compression
Training Data
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/load-balancing.title: load-balancing
agentic-coding/21-mlops/load-balancing.content:
Load Balancing

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Distributing requests across multiple model instances. Prevents any single instance from being overwhelmed.
📋 Concrete Example
Load balancer: 10,000 requests/minute. Distribute across 5 model instances: 2,000 each. No single instance is overloaded. Smooth operation.
🔗 Analogy
A school cafeteria with multiple lines - instead of one long line, students spread across 5 lines. Faster for everyone. Load balancing spreads requests across instances.
Related Concepts

Model Serving
Scalability
Throughput

agentic-coding/21-mlops/mlops.title: mlops
agentic-coding/21-mlops/mlops.content:
MLOps

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Machine Learning Operations - deploying, monitoring, and maintaining ML models in production. Like DevOps but for ML.
📋 Concrete Example
MLOps: 1) Train model. 2) Package as Docker image. 3) Deploy to Kubernetes. 4) Monitor performance. 5) Retrain when performance drops. Full lifecycle management.
🔗 Analogy
A restaurant kitchen - the chef creates the dish (training), the kitchen staff plates and serves it (deployment), the manager monitors quality (monitoring), and the menu updates when needed (retraining). MLOps runs the AI kitchen.
Related Concepts

Model Deployment
Monitoring
CI-CD

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-compressio.title: model-compression
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-compressio.content:
Model Compression

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Making models smaller and faster: quantization, pruning, distillation. Essential for edge deployment.
📋 Concrete Example
Compression: 175B parameter model -> 7B parameter model (via distillation). 95% smaller, 85% of original accuracy. Can run on a phone.
🔗 Analogy
Compressing a large file into a zip - much smaller, same content. Model compression makes models smaller while keeping most of their capability.
Related Concepts

Quantization
Pruning
Knowledge Distillation

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-deployment.title: model-deployment
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-deployment.content:
Model Deployment

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Making a trained model available for use. The model goes from development to production.
📋 Concrete Example
Deployment: model packaged as API. Users send requests: POST /predict {text: Hello}. Model returns: {sentiment: positive}. The model is now live.
🔗 Analogy
Opening a new store - you built the shop, stocked the shelves, trained the staff. Now you open the doors to customers. Model deployment opens the model to users.
Related Concepts

MLOps
API Endpoint
Serving

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-lifecycle.title: model-lifecycle
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-lifecycle.content:
Model Lifecycle

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
The full life of a model: conception -> data collection -> training -> evaluation -> deployment -> monitoring -> retraining -> retirement.
📋 Concrete Example
Lifecycle: v1 trained (Jan) -> deployed (Feb) -> monitored -> drift detected (May) -> retrained -> v2 deployed (Jun) -> … -> deprecated (2027). Full journey.
🔗 Analogy
A product lifecycle - design -> manufacture -> launch -> monitor -> improve -> relaunch -> discontinue. A model lifecycle is the product lifecycle for AI.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Model Versioning
Retraining

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-monitoring.title: model-monitoring
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-monitoring.content:
Model Monitoring

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Tracking model performance in production: accuracy, latency, usage, errors. Detects problems early.
📋 Concrete Example
Monitoring dashboard: accuracy 88% (stable), latency 200ms (good), 10K requests/hour, 0.1% error rate. All green. If accuracy drops to 80%, alert!
🔗 Analogy
A dashboard in a car - speed, fuel, engine temperature. You monitor constantly while driving. Model monitoring is the dashboard for AI in production.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Drift Detection
Alerting

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-optimizati.title: model-optimization
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-optimizati.content:
Model Optimization

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Making models faster, smaller, and cheaper to run. Includes quantization, pruning, distillation, and architectural improvements.
📋 Concrete Example
Optimization plan: 1) Quantize to 8-bit (-75% size). 2) Prune 30% neurons (-30% size). 3) Distill to smaller model (-90% size). Total: 96% smaller, 3% accuracy loss.
🔗 Analogy
Tuning a car for racing - lighter parts, better aerodynamics, optimized engine. Same car, much faster. Model optimization makes models faster and cheaper.
Related Concepts

Model Compression
Quantization
Pruning

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-pipeline.title: model-pipeline
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-pipeline.content:
Model Pipeline

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
The automated flow: data ingestion -> preprocessing -> training -> evaluation -> deployment -> monitoring.
📋 Concrete Example
Pipeline: 1) Fetch new data hourly. 2) Preprocess. 3) Retrain weekly. 4) Evaluate. 5) Deploy if better. 6) Monitor continuously. Fully automated ML lifecycle.
🔗 Analogy
An irrigation system - water flows from source -> filter -> distribute -> monitor -> adjust. Automated end-to-end. A model pipeline automates the ML lifecycle.
Related Concepts

MLOps
CI-CD
Automation

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-registry.title: model-registry
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-registry.content:
Model Registry

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
A centralized store for trained models: versions, metadata, performance metrics. Like a library for models.
📋 Concrete Example
Registry: {model: sentiment-v1, accuracy: 88%, date: 2025-01-01, status: production}. {model: sentiment-v2, accuracy: 91%, date: 2025-03-01, status: staging}. All versions tracked.
🔗 Analogy
A library catalog - each book has metadata (title, author, date, location). A model registry catalogs models with their metadata and versions.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Model Versioning
Metadata

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-serving.title: model-serving
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-serving.content:
Model Serving

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Running a model so it can process requests. Can be local, cloud, or edge.
📋 Concrete Example
Serving options: 1) Local: model on your laptop. 2) Cloud: model on AWS/GCP. 3) Edge: model on a phone. Each has different speed, cost, and privacy trade-offs.
🔗 Analogy
A food truck vs a restaurant vs a vending machine - different ways to serve food (model). Food truck (cloud), restaurant (local server), vending machine (edge). Each serves differently.
Related Concepts

Model Deployment
API Endpoint
Inference

agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-versioning.title: model-versioning
agentic-coding/21-mlops/model-versioning.content:
Model Versioning

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Tracking model versions over time. Each retrain creates a new version with updated performance.
📋 Concrete Example
Versioning: v1 (Jan, 88%), v2 (Mar, 91%), v3 (Jun, 93%). If v3 has a bug, rollback to v2. Versioning enables safe updates and rollbacks.
🔗 Analogy
Software updates on your phone - iOS 17.1, 17.2, 17.3. Each version is tracked. If 17.3 has a bug, you can downgrade. Model versioning works the same way.
Related Concepts

Model Registry
MLOps
Rollback

agentic-coding/21-mlops/observability.title: observability
agentic-coding/21-mlops/observability.content:
Observability

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Monitoring not just performance but internal model behavior: attention patterns, activation distributions, error patterns.
📋 Concrete Example
Observability: ‘Layer 5 activations are unusually high on certain inputs.’ This insight helps debug why the model makes specific errors. Deep visibility.
🔗 Analogy
An X-ray for a patient - you see inside the body, not just external symptoms. Observability sees inside the model, not just input-output.
Related Concepts

Model Monitoring
Debugging
Interpretability

agentic-coding/21-mlops/pruning.title: pruning
agentic-coding/21-mlops/pruning.content:
Pruning

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Removing unimportant neurons or connections. Smaller model, minimal accuracy loss.
📋 Concrete Example
Pruning: remove 30% of neurons with the smallest weights. Model size: -30%. Speed: +40%. Accuracy: 88% -> 87%. Minimal loss for big gains.
🔗 Analogy
Trimming a tree - cut dead branches. The tree is smaller but healthier. Pruning removes unimportant parts of the model.
Related Concepts

Model Compression
Neural Network
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/quantization.title: quantization
agentic-coding/21-mlops/quantization.content:
Quantization

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Reducing precision: 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers. Smaller model, faster inference, slight accuracy loss.
📋 Concrete Example
Quantization: 32-bit weights -> 8-bit weights. Model size: 1GB -> 250MB. Speed: 2x faster. Accuracy: 88% -> 86%. Worth the trade-off for edge deployment.
🔗 Analogy
Rounding numbers - 3.14159 -> 3.14. Slightly less precise but much easier to work with. Quantization rounds model weights for efficiency.
Related Concepts

Model Compression
Inference
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/random-search.title: random-search
agentic-coding/21-mlops/random-search.content:
Random Search

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Randomly sampling hyperparameter combinations. Often as good as grid search but faster.
📋 Concrete Example
Random search: try 20 random combinations. Found: lr=0.0015, batch=48 -> 89%. Faster than grid search, similar results. Efficient.
🔗 Analogy
Tasting random dishes at a buffet - instead of every combination, try 20 random ones. Often finds a great dish faster. Random search is efficient.
Related Concepts

Hyperparameter Tuning
Grid Search
Efficiency

agentic-coding/21-mlops/retraining.title: retraining
agentic-coding/21-mlops/retraining.content:
Retraining

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Training the model again with new data. Essential when drift is detected or new data is available.
📋 Concrete Example
Retraining: monthly. New data from the past month is added. Model retrains. New version: v4 (Jul, 92%). Deployed. Performance maintained.
🔗 Analogy
A student reviewing new material each month - they learn new things and update their knowledge. Retraining updates the model with new data.
Related Concepts

Drift Detection
Model Versioning
Training Data

agentic-coding/21-mlops/rollback.title: rollback
agentic-coding/21-mlops/rollback.content:
Rollback

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Reverting to a previous model version when the new version has problems. Quick recovery from bad deployments.
📋 Concrete Example
New model v3 deployed. Error rate jumps from 0.1% to 5%. Rollback to v2 immediately. Users are unaffected. v3 is fixed and redeployed later.
🔗 Analogy
Ctrl+Z in a word processor - you made a change that broke everything. Undo (rollback) to the previous version. Quick recovery.
Related Concepts

Model Versioning
Canary Deployment
Error Recovery

agentic-coding/21-mlops/scalability.title: scalability
agentic-coding/21-mlops/scalability.content:
Scalability

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
The ability to handle more requests by adding more resources. Critical for growing AI applications.
📋 Concrete Example
Scale: 100 users -> 1 model instance. 10,000 users -> 100 instances. Auto-scaling adds instances as demand grows. Handles any load.
🔗 Analogy
A restaurant expanding - 10 customers: 1 waiter. 100 customers: 10 waiters. Scales with demand. Model scalability adds instances as user demand grows.
Related Concepts

Load Balancing
Throughput
Auto-Scaling

agentic-coding/21-mlops/serving-infrastr.title: serving-infrastructure
agentic-coding/21-mlops/serving-infrastr.content:
Serving Infrastructure

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
The hardware and software stack that runs models in production: GPUs, servers, load balancers, APIs.
📋 Concrete Example
Infrastructure: 10 GPU servers behind a load balancer, serving API requests. Kubernetes manages pods. Prometheus monitors. Complete serving stack.
🔗 Analogy
A restaurant’s kitchen infrastructure - stoves, ovens, refrigerators, dishwashers, ventilation. The full hardware and software for cooking. Serving infrastructure runs models.
Related Concepts

Model Serving
MLOps
Scalability

agentic-coding/21-mlops/sla.title: sla
agentic-coding/21-mlops/sla.content:
SLA

Domain: MLOps

🎯 Motivation
Service Level Agreement - a promise about model performance: 99.9% uptime, <200ms latency. If violated, consequences.
📋 Concrete Example
SLA: 99.9% uptime (max 43 min downtime/month), <200ms latency (99% of requests), <0.1% error rate. If violated, customers get refunds. Binding promise.
🔗 Analogy
A delivery guarantee - ‘30 minutes or free.’ The restaurant promises a delivery time. An SLA promises model performance.
Related Concepts

MLOps
Reliability
Monitoring

hermes-agent/01-fundamentals/agent-loop.title: agent-loop
hermes-agent/01-fundamentals/agent-loop.content:
Agent Loop

Domain: Hermes Fundamentals

Motivation
The agent loop is the heartbeat of Hermes. It goes: think, act, observe, repeat. Hermes receives your request, decides a tool to use, reads the result, then decides the next step until the task is done.
Concrete Example
You ask Hermes to find the cheapest phone plan. It searches the web (act), reads the results (observe), compares prices (think), then answers. That is one full loop.
Analogy
Like playing a turn-based game: you pick a move, see what happens, then plan your next move.

hermes-agent/01-fundamentals/ai-agent-vs.content:
AI Agent vs Chatbot

Domain: Hermes Fundamentals

Motivation
A chatbot only replies with text. An AI agent can also take actions, such as running code, editing files, or sending messages. This difference is why Hermes can actually finish tasks, not just talk about them.
Concrete Example
A chatbot tells you how to convert a video. Hermes actually runs the conversion command and hands you the new file.
Analogy
A chatbot is like a friend who gives directions. An agent is like a friend who walks with you to the destination.

Autonomous Agent

Domain: Hermes Fundamentals

Motivation
An autonomous agent can decide what steps to take on its own, without you spelling out every command. You give it a goal, and it figures out which tools to use and in what order.
Concrete Example
You tell Hermes to back up your project folder to a USB drive. Hermes checks the folder size, copies the files, and confirms the backup finished.
Analogy
Like a delivery rider who, once you give the address, picks the fastest route and delivers the food without you guiding every turn.

The browser toolset lets Hermes control a real web browser, clicking buttons and filling forms. This is needed for websites that require login or have dynamic content that simple search cannot reach.

Checkpoints

Domain: Hermes Fundamentals

Motivation
Checkpoints are snapshots of your files at a moment in time. If Hermes makes a mess of your project, you can roll back to the last checkpoint and try again.
Concrete Example
Hermes edits five files to add a feature. It goes wrong. You type /rollback and the files return to how they were.
Analogy
Like a save point in a video game. If you die, you respawn at the save point.

Command Approval

Motivation
For safety, Hermes asks for your permission before running commands that could be destructive, like deleting files. You can also set it to auto-approve low-risk commands.
Concrete Example
Hermes wants to run rm old_files. It shows you the command and waits for you to type yes before executing.

Like a bank app that asks you to confirm before transferring money. It protects you from mistakes.

Context Compression

Motivation
Conversations can get long and exceed the model memory limit. Hermes automatically compresses older context, keeping the important points and dropping the rest, so the chat can continue.
Concrete Example
After a 200-message conversation, Hermes summarises the first 150 messages into a short paragraph and keeps the recent 50 messages in full.
Analogy
Like skimming the first chapters of a book so you can focus on the current chapter, without forgetting the plot.

You add three OpenAI keys. Hermes uses the first until it hits the limit, then seamlessly switches to the second.
Analogy
Like having multiple Octopus cards in your wallet. When one runs out of money, you tap the next one.

Delegation Tool

Hermes can spawn sub-agents to work on sub-tasks in parallel. This is called delegation. The parent agent waits for the children to finish, then combines their results.
Concrete Example
You ask Hermes to research three phone models. It spawns three sub-agents, each researching one phone, then merges the comparisons.

Learning Loop

Motivation
The learning loop is how Hermes turns experience into reusable knowledge. When it finishes a hard task, it may save the steps as a skill. Over time, these skills stack up and Hermes becomes faster.
Concrete Example
Hermes spends ten minutes figuring out how to scrape a website. It saves a skill. Next week, the same task takes thirty seconds.
Analogy
Like practising a song on the piano. The first time is slow and full of mistakes. After a week, your fingers just know where to go.

Hermes is on turn 85 of a complex research task. It knows it has 5 turns left and starts wrapping up its answer.

Hermes remembers facts about you and your environment across conversations. This means you do not have to reintroduce yourself every time. Memory makes interactions feel continuous.

On Monday you tell Hermes your name is Alex. On Friday, Hermes greets you as Alex without being reminded.

Like translators at a meeting. Each one speaks a different language but passes the same message to the boss.

A profile is a separate Hermes instance with its own config, sessions, skills, and memory. You can have one for school, one for gaming, one for experiments. They never mix.

Hermes gets better the more you use it. When it solves a tricky problem or learns a new workflow, it can save that knowledge as a skill. Next time it faces the same task, it loads the skill and works faster.

Terminal Agent

Motivation
The most common way to use Hermes is in a terminal, a text-based screen where you type commands. This is fast, lightweight, and works on almost any computer, even a cheap server.

Motivation
Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent made by Nous Research. Unlike a chatbot that only talks, Hermes can run commands, read and write files, search the web, and remember things across conversations. It lives in your terminal, on your phone through messaging apps, or on a server.
Concrete Example
You type a message asking Hermes to summarise your homework notes into bullet points. Hermes reads the files, writes a summary file, and tells you it is done.

Three things set Hermes apart: it learns from experience (skills), it remembers you across sessions (memory), and it runs on many platforms at once. Most chatbots do none of these.

After a week of use, Hermes knows you prefer Python, remembers your school project folder, and can fix bugs in code it helped you write before.

Like a tutor who has taught you for months and knows your strengths, versus a stranger you meet once.

A health check at the doctor - they run tests on everything and tell you what is fine and what needs attention. Skills check does a health check on your skill library.

Skills Command

Motivation
A slash command that lists all available skills in the current session, showing which are loaded and which are available to load.

Typing /skills shows: Loaded: debugging, tdd / Available: github-pr-workflow, dockerfile-optimization. You see what is active and what you can activate.

Opening your backpack and seeing what is inside - some books are already on your desk (loaded), others are in the bag (available). /skills shows your skill inventory.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-con.content:
Skills Config

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Configuring skill settings: which directories to scan, whether auto-discovery is on, and other preferences.
Concrete Example
hermes skills config shows: skills_dirs: [~/.hermes/skills, ./skills] / auto_discover: true / max_skills: 100. You can change these to fit your setup.

Settings on your phone - you configure which apps can send notifications, how they are grouped, and where they appear. Skills config sets up how skills behave.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-hub.title: skills-hub
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-hub.content:
Skills Hub

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
A central online repository where the community shares skills. Think of it as an app store for agent skills.
Concrete Example
The hub has hundreds of skills: github tools, docker helpers, creative generators. You search, install, and use. Popular skills get many installs and reviews.
Analogy
The Apple App Store or Google Play Store - a central place where developers publish apps and users download them. The skills hub is the app store for agent skills.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-ins.content:
Skills Inspect

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Looking at the details of a skill before using it - what it does, what files it contains, and how it works.
Concrete Example
hermes skills inspect debugging shows: Name: debugging / Description: 4-phase root cause debugging / Files: SKILL.md, scripts/trace.sh / Author: agent. You see the full picture.
Analogy
Reading the back of a box before buying - ingredients, instructions, warnings. Skills inspect shows you what is inside a skill before you commit to using it.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-ins.content:
Skills Install

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Adding a new skill to your agent from the skills hub or a local path. After install, the agent can use it immediately.
Concrete Example
hermes skills install github-pr-workflow downloads the skill from the hub, places it in the skills directory, and confirms: Installed github-pr-workflow successfully.

Downloading an app from the App Store - you tap install, it downloads and appears on your phone ready to use. Skills install does this for agent skills.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-lis.content:
Skills List

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
The command to see all installed skills at a glance. Shows skill names and short descriptions so you know what is available.
Concrete Example
Running hermes skills list outputs: github-pr-workflow - Branch, commit, open PR / debugging - Systematic 4-phase debugging / tdd - Test-driven development. A quick inventory.

Checking your phone’s app drawer - you see all installed apps with their icons and names. Skills list shows all installed skills with names and descriptions.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-pub.title: skills-publish
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-pub.content:
Skills Publish

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Sharing a skill you created with the community by uploading it to the skills hub so others can install and use it.
Concrete Example
You created a great skill for Moodle plugin testing. hermes skills publish moodle-plugin-testing uploads it to the hub. Others can now hermes skills install it.

Publishing a recipe on a cooking website - you share your dish so anyone in the world can try it. Skills publish shares your skill with the whole community.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-sea.title: skills-search
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-sea.content:
Skills Search

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
When you have many skills, searching by keyword finds the right one faster than scrolling through a long list.
Concrete Example
hermes skills search deploy finds: k8s-troubleshooting, vllm-deployment, helm-chart-deployment. Searching docker finds dockerfile-optimization and k8s-troubleshooting.

Using a search bar in an app store - instead of scrolling through thousands of apps, you type deploy and see only deployment-related results.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-tap.title: skills-tap
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-tap.content:
Skills Tap

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Adding a source repository to your skills hub so you can install skills from that source. Tapping is like adding a new store.
Concrete Example
hermes skills tap nousresearch/skills adds the Nous Research skill repository as a source. Now you can install skills from that repo alongside the default hub.
Analogy
Adding a new bookstore to your reading app - previously you only had one store. Now you tap to add another, so you can browse and buy from both.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-uni.title: skills-uninstall
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-uni.content:
Skills Uninstall

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Removing a skill you no longer need. Keeps the skill library clean and saves space.
Concrete Example
hermes skills uninstall old-python-2-tool removes the skill files and confirms removal. The agent will no longer load or suggest this skill.
Analogy
Deleting an app from your phone - press and hold, tap delete, it is gone. Skills uninstall removes a skill you do not need anymore.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-upd.title: skills-update
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/skills-upd.content:
Skills Update

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Fetching the latest version of skills from the hub. Skills get improved over time, and update keeps you current.
Concrete Example
hermes skills update checks all installed skills for newer versions. If github-pr-workflow has a v2, it downloads and replaces the old version. You get bug fixes and improvements.

Updating apps on your phone - developers release new versions with fixes and features. You tap update to get the latest. Skills update does this for agent skills.

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/stale-skil.title: stale-skills
hermes-agent/07-skills-system/stale-skil.content:
Stale Skills

Domain: Skills System

Motivation
Skills that have not been used in a long time. They clutter the library and may contain outdated instructions. The curator identifies and archives them.
Concrete Example
A skill called old-docker-compose was last used 4 months ago. The curator flags it as stale. If still unused, it gets archived to keep the library clean.
Analogy
Food in the fridge that is past its expiry date - it takes up space and might not be good anymore. Stale skills take up space and may be outdated.

Skill Lifecycle

hermes-agent/07-skills-system/usage-json.content:
Usage JSON

Motivation
A small file (.usage.json) next to each skill that records usage statistics: times used, last used date, success rate.

debugging/.usage.json contains: {used_count: 42, last_used: 2026-08-03, success_rate: 0.88}. The curator reads this to decide if the skill is stale.

A mileage log in a car - it tracks total miles, last trip date, fuel efficiency. .usage.json tracks a skill usage stats the same way.

AGENTS.md

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A file that tells the agent about the project: what it is, conventions to follow, and things to watch out for. Like a briefing document.
Concrete Example
AGENTS.md says: This is a Flask web app. Use Python 3.11. Tests go in tests/. Never commit to main branch. The agent follows these rules when working on the project.

A briefing packet for a new employee - here is the project, here are the rules, here is what to watch out for. AGENTS.md briefs the agent on the project.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/built-in-.title: built-in-memory
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/built-in-.content:
Built-in Memory

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
The default memory provider. Stores memories locally in files. Simple, no setup needed, but limited features.
Concrete Example
Built-in memory saves facts to MEMORY.md and USER.md on your machine. No external service needed. It works out of the box but does not have smart search or sharing.
Analogy
A notebook you keep in your bag - always there, no internet needed, but you have to flip through pages manually. Built-in memory is the simple local notebook.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/claudemd.content:
CLAUDE.md

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A context file originally for Claude Code but widely adopted. Tells the agent coding standards, style preferences, and project-specific instructions.
Concrete Example
CLAUDE.md contains: Use 4-space indentation. Add type hints to all functions. Prefer composition over inheritance. The agent follows these when writing code.
Analogy
A style guide for a school newspaper - headline rules, font size, citation format. Writers follow it for consistency. CLAUDE.md is a style guide for the agent.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/compress-.content:
Compress Command

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A slash command that manually triggers context compression. Useful when you know the conversation is long and want to compress before the automatic threshold.
Concrete Example
Typing /compress immediately summarizes older messages. The agent shows: Compressed 30 messages into a summary. Context now at 40 percent. You have room to continue.
Analogy
Pressing save on a document to reduce its working state - you compress the history into a saved version. /compress compresses conversation history manually.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/compressi.title: compression-threshold
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/compressi.content:
Compression Threshold

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
The point at which context compression triggers. When the conversation length exceeds this threshold, the agent compresses automatically.
Concrete Example
Threshold set to 80 percent of context window. When the conversation fills 80 percent, compression kicks in. Below that, no compression needed.
Analogy
A water tank alarm - when water reaches 80 percent capacity, the alarm triggers. The compression threshold triggers when context reaches its limit.

Context Compression
Target Ratio

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-b.title: context-budget
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-b.content:
Context Budget

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
The total context space available. The agent must budget it across system prompt, memory, conversation, and files. Running out means compression or loss.
Concrete Example
Budget: 128K tokens. System prompt: 2K, memory: 5K, conversation: 100K, files: 21K. Total: 128K. If conversation grows, something else must shrink (compression).
Analogy
A monthly allowance - you budget across food, transport, and fun. If one grows, another shrinks. Context budget allocates tokens across all context sources.

Context Window
Context Prioritisation

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-c.title: context-compression
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-c.content:
Context Compression

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
When a conversation gets very long, the agent compresses older messages into a summary to fit within its context window. You keep the meaning but use less space.
Concrete Example
After 50 messages, the agent compresses messages 1-40 into: User asked about Python lists, dicts, and loops. Decided to build a calculator. Now the context has room for new messages.
Analogy
Summarising a long meeting into bullet points - instead of keeping the full 2-hour transcript, you write 5 key points. Same information, much less space.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-f.title: context-files
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-f.content:
Context Files

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Files the agent reads at the start of each session to get context: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules. They set rules and provide project context.
Concrete Example
The agent starts a session, reads AGENTS.md (project conventions), CLAUDE.md (coding standards). Now it knows the project rules before you even ask a question.
Analogy
Reading the house rules when you check into a hotel - wifi password, breakfast time, checkout. Before you start your stay, you read the rules. Context files are the house rules.

AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-f.title: context-freshness
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-f.content:
Context Freshness

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Recent context is more relevant than old context. The agent weights recent messages and memory higher when deciding what matters now.
Concrete Example
You switched from Python to JavaScript last week. The agent weights this recent switch higher than your Python preferences from 3 months ago. Freshness keeps the agent current.
Analogy
News - today headlines matter more than last week. The agent treats recent context as more relevant, like how you prioritise recent news.
Related Concepts

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-i.title: context-injection
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-i.content:
Context Injection

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Automatically inserting relevant context (memories, files, past session info) into the conversation before the agent responds.
Concrete Example
You ask: Help me continue my project. The agent injects: your project details from MEMORY.md, your skills from USER.md, and the last session summary. Now it has full context to help.
Analogy
A waiter who knows your usual order - before you speak, they already know you want the set lunch with iced tea. Context injection pre-loads what the agent needs.

Context Files

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-l.title: context-loss
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-l.content:
Context Loss

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
When information falls out of the context window and is forgotten. Compression helps, but some detail is always lost in very long conversations.
Concrete Example
After a 200-message conversation, the agent does not remember the exact code from message 5. It remembers the summary (you were debugging a sort function) but not the exact code.
Analogy
Forgetting the beginning of a long movie by the end - you remember the plot but not every line of dialogue. Context loss is the agent forgetting old details.
Related Concepts

Context Window
Context Compression
Compression Threshold

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-p.title: context-prioritisation
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-p.content:
Context Prioritisation

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
When context is limited, the agent prioritises what to keep: recent messages, important memories, and active instructions come first.
Concrete Example
With limited context, the agent keeps: the last 10 messages (recent), your user profile (important), and the current task instruction (active). Old tangents get compressed first.
Analogy
Packing a backpack for a hike - you pack the essentials first (water, map, first aid), then nice-to-haves. Context prioritisation packs the most important context first.

Context Window
Context Compression
Memory Retrieval

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-r.title: context-references
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-r.content:
Context References

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Ways the agent can pull in external context: file references, URL references, and session links. This extends what the agent knows beyond the conversation.
Concrete Example
You type: Look at @agents.md and @session:work/42. The agent reads AGENTS.md for project rules and session 42 for past context. References pull in extra information.
Analogy
Footnotes in a book - they reference other pages or sources. You flip to them for more context. Context references let the agent pull in external context.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-s.title: context-snapshot
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-s.content:
Context Snapshot

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A saved snapshot of the current context (messages, memory, files) at a point in time. Useful for debugging or resuming.
Concrete Example
Before a risky operation, the agent saves a context snapshot. If something goes wrong, it can roll back to this snapshot and try a different approach.
Analogy
A save point in a video game - before a boss fight, you save. If you lose, you reload from the save point. Context snapshots are save points for agent context.

Context Loss
Context Budget

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-w.title: context-window
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/context-w.content:
Context Window

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
The maximum amount of text the agent can consider at once. Like short-term memory - it holds the current conversation but has a limit.
Concrete Example
If the context window is 128K tokens (about 100,000 words), and your conversation is 150,000 words, the oldest messages fall out of the window and are forgotten unless compressed.
Analogy
A person short-term memory - you can hold a conversation in mind, but if it goes on for hours, the earliest parts fade. The context window is the agent short-term memory.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/cursor-ru.content:
Cursor Rules

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A file (.cursorrules) that defines how the agent should behave in a project. Originally for Cursor IDE but can be read by other agents.
Concrete Example
.cursorrules says: Always write tests before implementation. Use descriptive variable names. Comment complex logic. The agent treats these as rules to follow.
Analogy
Rules posted in a computer lab - no food, log off when done, save files to the shared drive. Cursor rules are the lab rules for the agent.

Context Files
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/honcho-me.title: honcho-memory
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/honcho-me.content:
Honcho Memory

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A memory provider that lets multiple agents share the same memory. Good for teams where several agents help the same user.
Concrete Example
With Honcho, agent A learns you like Python, and agent B (using the same Honcho) also knows this. Shared memory means consistent service across multiple agents.

A shared family calendar - when mom adds an event, dad and kids all see it. Honcho memory lets multiple agents share what they know about you.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/mem0-memo.title: mem0-memory
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/mem0-memo.content:
Mem0 Memory

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A smart memory provider that uses AI to organise, summarise, and retrieve memories intelligently. Finds relevant memories even with fuzzy queries.
Concrete Example
Mem0 stores 100 facts about you. You ask about your coding project. Mem0 finds the 3 relevant memories (your Python level, your project topic, your deadline) and surfaces them.
Analogy
A smart photo album that tags faces and places - when you search beach, it finds all beach photos even without that word in the filename. Mem0 finds relevant memories smartly.

Built-in Memory

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ac.title: memory-accuracy
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ac.content:
Memory Accuracy

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Ensuring stored memories are correct. Inaccurate memories lead to wrong personalisation. The agent verifies before saving.
Concrete Example
Agent hears: I got a B on my math test. It saves: User received a B on the math test (verified from user statement). It does not guess or assume details it was not told.
Analogy
A journalist fact-checking before publishing - they verify the claim before printing it. Memory accuracy means the agent saves only verified facts.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ad.title: memory-add
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ad.content:
Memory Add

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Adding a new fact to memory. The agent does this when it learns something new and worth remembering.
Concrete Example
Agent learns: User has a dog named Rex. It calls memory add: User has a dog named Rex. Now every future session knows about Rex.
Analogy
Writing a new entry in your diary - today I learned something new, so I add it. Memory add writes a new fact into the agent memory.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ba.title: memory-batch-operations
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ba.content:
Memory Batch Operations

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
Adding, replacing, or removing multiple memories in one action. Faster than doing them one at a time.
Concrete Example
The agent learns 5 things in one conversation. Instead of 5 separate memory calls, it batches: add 3, replace 1, remove 1. One operation, multiple changes.
Analogy
Going to the grocery store with a list - instead of 5 trips for 5 items, you do one trip and get everything. Batch operations handle multiple memories at once.

hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ch.title: memory-char-limit
hermes-agent/08-memory-context/memory-ch.content:
Memory Char Limit

Domain: Memory & Context

Motivation
A maximum character count for each memory entry. Prevents overly long memories that bloat files and slow loading.
Concrete Example
A memory entry is limited to 500 characters. The agent wants to save a long story but must compress it: User is building a Flask chatbot for a school project. Concise and under the limit.
Analogy
Twitter character limit - you cannot write an essay in a tweet. You must be concise. Memory char limit forces the agent to be brief and clear.

Memory Operations
MEMORY.md
